texts.ecc.2.21: Porque ha homem que trabalha com sabedoria, e sciencia, e destreza; todavia deixará o seu trabalho, como porção sua, a um homem que não trabalhou n’elle: tambem isto é vaidade e grande enfado.
texts.ecc.2.22: Porque, que mais tem o homem de todo o seu trabalho, e fadiga do seu coração, em que elle anda trabalhando debaixo do sol?
texts.ecc.2.23: Porque todos os seus dias são dôres, e a sua occupação é vexação; até de noite não descança o seu coração: tambem isto é vaidade.
texts.ecc.2.24: Não é pois bom para o homem que coma e beba, e que faça gozar a sua alma do bem do seu trabalho? tambem eu vi que isto vem da mão de Deus.
texts.ecc.2.25: (Porque quem pode comer, ou quem o pode gozar melhor do que eu?).
texts.ecc.2.26: Porque ao homem que é bom diante d’elle dá Deus sabedoria e conhecimento e alegria, porém ao peccador dá trabalho, para que elle ajunte, e amontoe, para o dar ao bom perante a sua face. Tambem isto é vaidade e afflicção d’espirito.
texts.ecc.3.1: Tudo tem o seu tempo determinado, e todo o proposito debaixo do céu tem o seu tempo:
texts.ecc.3.2: Ha tempo de nascer, e tempo de morrer: tempo de plantar, e tempo d’arrancar o que se plantou:
texts.ecc.3.3: Tempo de matar, e tempo de curar: tempo de derribar, e tempo de edificar:
texts.ecc.3.4: Tempo de chorar, e tempo de rir: tempo de prantear, e tempo de saltar:
texts.ecc.3.5: Tempo de espalhar pedras, e tempo de ajuntar pedras: tempo de abraçar, e tempo de afastar-se de abraçar:
texts.ecc.3.6: Tempo de buscar, e tempo de perder: tempo de guardar, e tempo de deitar fóra:
texts.ecc.3.7: Tempo de rasgar, e tempo de coser: tempo de calar, e tempo de fallar:
texts.ecc.3.8: Tempo de amar, e tempo de aborrecer: tempo de guerra, e tempo de paz.
texts.ecc.3.9: Que vantagem tem o trabalhador d’aquillo em que trabalha?
texts.ecc.3.10: Tenho visto o trabalho que Deus deu aos filhos dos homens, para com elle os affligir.
texts.ecc.3.11: Tudo fez formoso em seu tempo: tambem poz o seculo no coração d’elles, sem que o homem possa descobrir a obra que Deus fez desde o principio até ao fim.
texts.ecc.3.12: Já tenho advertido que não ha coisa melhor para elles do que alegrar-se e fazer bem na sua vida;
texts.ecc.3.13: Como tambem que todo o homem coma e beba, e goze do bem de todo o seu trabalho: isto é um dom de Deus.
texts.ecc.3.14: Sei eu que tudo quanto Deus faz isso durará eternamente: nada se lhe deve accrescentar, e nada d’elle se deve diminuir; e isto faz Deus para que haja temor diante d’elle.
texts.ecc.3.15: O que houve d’antes ainda o ha agora: e o que ha de ser, já foi; e Deus pede conta do que passou.
texts.ecc.3.16: Vi mais debaixo do sol, no logar do juizo, que havia ali impiedade, e no logar da justiça que ali havia impiedade.
texts.ecc.3.17: Eu disse no meu coração: Deus julgará o justo e o impio; porque ali será o tempo para julgar de todo o intento e sobre toda a obra.
texts.ecc.3.18: Disse eu no meu coração ácerca do estado dos filhos dos homens, que Deus lhes declararia; e elles o veriam, que elles são como as bestas em si mesmos.
texts.ecc.3.19: Porque o que succede aos filhos dos homens, isso mesmo tambem succede ás bestas, e o mesmo succede a elles ambos: como morre um, assim morre o outro; e todos teem o mesmo folego, e a vantagem dos homens sobre as bestas não é nenhuma, porque todos são vaidade.
texts.ecc.3.20: Todos vão para um logar: todos foram feitos do pó, e todos voltarão ao pó.
texts.ecc.3.21: Quem adverte que o folego dos filhos dos homens sobe para cima, e que o folego das bestas desce para baixo da terra?
texts.ecc.3.22: Assim que tenho visto que não ha coisa melhor do que alegrar-se o homem nas suas obras, porque essa é a sua porção; porque quem o levará a vêr o que será depois d’elle?
texts.ecc.4.1: Depois me virei, e attentei em todas as oppressões que se fazem debaixo do sol; e eis que vi as lagrimas dos que foram opprimidos e dos que não teem consolador; e a força estava da banda dos seus oppressores; porém elles não tinham consolador.
texts.ecc.4.2: Pelo que eu louvei os mortos que já morreram, mais do que os vivos que vivem ainda,
texts.ecc.4.3: E melhor que uns e outros é aquelle que ainda não é; que não viu as más obras que se fazem debaixo do sol.
texts.ecc.4.4: Tambem vi eu que todo o trabalho, e toda a destreza em obras, attrahe ao homem a inveja do seu proximo. Tambem isto é vaidade e afflicção d’espirito.
texts.ecc.4.5: O tolo cruza as suas mãos, e come a sua propria carne.
texts.ecc.4.6: Melhor é uma mão cheia com descanço do que ambos os punhos cheios com trabalho, e afflicção d’espirito.
texts.ecc.4.7: Outra vez me tornei a virar, e vi uma vaidade debaixo do sol.
texts.ecc.4.8: Ha um tal que é só, e não tem segundo, nem tão pouco filho nem irmã; e de todo o seu trabalho não ha fim, nem o seu olho se farta de riquezas; nem diz: Para quem trabalho eu, e privo a minha alma do bem? Tambem isto é vaidade e enfadonha occupação.
texts.ecc.4.9: Melhores são dois do que um, porque teem melhor paga do seu trabalho.
texts.ecc.4.10: Porque se vierem a cair, um levanta ao seu companheiro: mas ai do que estiver só; pois, caindo, não haverá outro que o levante.
texts.ecc.4.11: Tambem, se dois dormirem juntos, elles se aquentarão; mas um só como se aquentará?
texts.ecc.4.12: E, se alguem prevalecer contra um, os dois lhe resistirão; e o cordão de tres dobras não se quebra tão depressa.
texts.ecc.4.13: Melhor é o mancebo pobre e sabio do que o rei velho e insensato, que se não deixa mais admoestar.
texts.ecc.4.14: Porque um sae do carcere para reinar; sim, um que nasceu pobre no seu reino.
texts.ecc.4.15: Vi a todos os viventes andarem debaixo do sol com o mancebo, o successor que estará no seu logar.
texts.ecc.4.16: Não tem fim todo o povo, todo o que houve antes d’elle; tão pouco os descendentes se alegrarão d’elle. Na verdade que tambem isto é vaidade e afflicção d’espirito.
texts.ecc.5.1: Guarda o teu pé, quando entrares na casa de Deus; e inclina-te mais a ouvir do que a offerecer sacrificios de tolos, pois não sabem que fazem mal.
texts.ecc.5.2: Não te precipites com a tua bocca, nem o teu coração se apresse a pronunciar palavra alguma diante de Deus; porque Deus está nos céus, e tu estás sobre a terra; pelo que sejam poucas as tuas palavras.
texts.ecc.5.3: Porque, da muita occupação vem os sonhos, e a voz do tolo da multidão das palavras.
texts.ecc.5.4: Quando a Deus fizeres algum voto, não tardes em cumpril-o; porque não se agrada de tolos: o que votares, paga-o.
texts.ecc.5.5: Melhor é que não votes do que votes e não pagues.
texts.ecc.5.6: Não consintas que a tua bocca faça peccar a tua carne, nem digas diante do anjo que foi erro: por que causa se iraria Deus contra a tua voz, que destruisse a obra das tuas mãos?
texts.ecc.5.7: Porque, como na multidão dos sonhos ha vaidades, assim o ha nas muitas palavras: mas tu teme a Deus.
texts.ecc.5.8: Se vires em alguma provincia oppressão de pobres, e violencia do juizo e da justiça, não te maravilhes de similhante caso; porque o que mais alto é do que os altos n’isso attenta; e ha mais altos do que elles.
texts.ecc.5.9: O proveito da terra é para todos: até o rei se serve do campo.
texts.ecc.5.10: O que amar o dinheiro nunca se fartará do dinheiro; e quem amar a abundancia nunca se fartará da renda: tambem isto é vaidade.
texts.ecc.5.11: Onde a fazenda se multiplica, ali se multiplicam tambem os que a comem: que mais proveito pois teem os seus donos do que verem-n’a com os seus olhos?
texts.ecc.5.12: Doce é o somno do trabalhador, quer coma pouco quer muito; porém a fartura do rico não o deixa dormir.
texts.ecc.5.13: Ha mal que vi debaixo do sol, e attrahe enfermidades: as riquezas que os seus donos guardam para o seu proprio mal;
texts.ecc.5.14: Porque as mesmas riquezas se perdem com enfadonhas occupações, e gerando algum filho nada lhe fica na sua mão.
texts.ecc.5.15: Como saiu do ventre de sua mãe, assim nú se tornará, indo-se como veiu; e nada tomará do seu trabalho, que possa levar na sua mão.
texts.ecc.5.16: Assim que tambem isto é um mal que attrahe enfermidades, que, infallivelmente, como veiu, assim se vae: e que proveito lhe vem de trabalhar para o vento,
texts.ecc.5.17: E de haver comido todos os seus dias nas trevas, e de padecer muito enfado, e enfermidade, e cruel furor?
texts.ecc.5.18: Eis aqui o que eu vi, uma boa e bella coisa: comer e beber, e gozar-se do bem de todo o seu trabalho, em que trabalhou debaixo do sol, durante o numero dos dias da sua vida que Deus lhe deu, porque esta é a sua porção.
texts.ecc.5.19: E todo o homem, a quem Deus deu riquezas e fazenda, e lhe deu poder para comer d’ellas, e tomar a sua porção, e gozar do seu trabalho: isto é dom de Deus.
texts.ecc.5.20: Porque não se lembrará muito dos dias da sua vida; porquanto Deus lhe responde com alegria do seu coração.
texts.ecc.6.1: Ha um mal que tenho visto debaixo do sol, e mui frequente é entre os homens:
texts.ecc.6.2: Um homem a quem Deus deu riquezas, fazenda e honra, e nada lhe falta de tudo quanto a sua alma deseja, e Deus não lhe dá poder para d’ahi comer, antes o estranho lh’o come: tambem isto é vaidade e uma má enfermidade.
texts.ecc.6.3: Se o homem gerar cem filhos, e viver muitos annos, e os dias dos seus annos forem muitos, porém a sua alma se não fartar do bem, e tambem não tiver sepultura, digo que um aborto é melhor do que elle.
texts.ecc.6.4: Porquanto debalde veiu, e ás trevas se vae, e de trevas se encobre o seu nome.
texts.ecc.6.5: E ainda que nunca viu o sol, nem o conheceu, mais descanço tem do que o tal.
texts.ecc.6.6: E, ainda que vivesse duas vezes mil annos e não visse o bem, porventura todos não vão para um mesmo logar?
texts.ecc.6.7: Todo o trabalho do homem é para a sua bocca, e comtudo nunca se enche a sua cubiça.
texts.ecc.6.8: Porque, que mais tem o sabio do que o tolo? e que mais tem o pobre que sabe andar perante os vivos?
texts.ecc.6.9: Melhor é a vista dos olhos do que o vaguear da cubiça: tambem isto é vaidade, e afflicção de espirito.
texts.ecc.6.10: Seja qualquer o que fôr, já o seu nome foi nomeado, e sabe-se que é homem, e que não póde contender com o que é mais forte do que elle.
texts.ecc.6.11: Na verdade que ha muitas coisas que multiplicam a vaidade: que mais tem o homem com ellas!
texts.ecc.6.12: Porque quem sabe o que é bom n’esta vida para o homem, durante o numero dos dias da vida da sua vaidade, os quaes gasta como sombra? porque quem declarará ao homem que é o que passará depois d’elle debaixo do sol?
texts.ecc.7.1: Melhor é a boa fama do que o melhor unguento, e o dia da morte do que o dia do nascimento d’alguem.
texts.ecc.7.2: Melhor é ir á casa do luto do que ir á casa do banquete, porque n’ella é o fim de todos os homens; e os vivos o applicam ao seu coração.
texts.ecc.7.3: Melhor é o nojo do que o riso, porque com a tristeza do rosto se encommenda o coração.
texts.ecc.7.4: O coração dos sabios está na casa do luto, mas o coração dos tolos na casa da alegria.
texts.ecc.7.5: Melhor é ouvir a reprehensão do sabio, do que ouvir alguem a canção do tolo.
texts.ecc.7.6: Porque qual o ruido dos espinhos debaixo d’uma panella, tal é o riso do tolo: tambem isto é vaidade.
texts.ecc.7.7: Verdadeiramente que a oppressão faria endoidecer até ao sabio, e a peita corrompe o coração.
texts.ecc.7.8: Melhor é o fim das coisas do que o principio d’ellas: melhor é o longanimo do que o altivo de coração.
texts.ecc.7.9: Não te apresses no teu espirito a irar-te, porque a ira repousa no seio dos tolos.
texts.ecc.7.10: Nunca digas: Porque foram os dias passados melhores do que estes? porque nunca com sabedoria isto perguntarias.
texts.ecc.7.11: Tão boa é a sabedoria como a herança, e d’ella os que vêem o sol tiram proveito.
texts.ecc.7.12: Porque a sabedoria serve de sombra, como de sombra serve o dinheiro; mas a excellencia do conhecimento é que a sabedoria dá vida ao seu possuidor.
texts.ecc.7.13: Attenta para a obra de Deus; porque quem poderá endireitar o que elle fez torto?
texts.ecc.7.14: No dia da prosperidade goza do bem, mas no dia da adversidade considera; porque tambem Deus fez a este em opposição áquelle, para que o homem nada ache do que haverá depois d’elle.
texts.ecc.7.15: Tudo isto vi nos dias da minha vaidade: ha um justo que perece na sua justiça, e ha um impio que prolonga os seus dias na sua maldade.
texts.ecc.7.16: Não sejas demasiadamente justo, nem demasiadamente sabio: para que te destruirias a ti mesmo?
texts.ecc.7.17: Não sejas demasiadamente impio, nem sejas demasiadamente louco: para que morrerias fóra de teu tempo?
texts.ecc.7.18: Bom é que retenhas isto, e tambem d’isto não retires a tua mão; porque quem teme a Deus escapa de tudo isto.
texts.ecc.7.19: A sabedoria fortalece ao sabio, mais do que dez governadores que haja na cidade.
texts.ecc.7.20: Na verdade que não ha homem justo sobre a terra, que faça bem, e nunca peque.
texts.ecc.7.21: Tão pouco appliques o teu coração a todas as palavras que se disserem, para que não venhas a ouvir que o teu servo te amaldiçoa.
texts.ecc.7.22: Porque o teu coração tambem já confessou muitas vezes que tambem tu amaldiçoaste a outros.
texts.ecc.7.23: Tudo isto inquiri com sabedoria; e disse: Sabedoria adquirirei; mas ella ainda estava longe de mim.
texts.ecc.7.24: Longe está o que foi; e o profundissimo quem o achará?
texts.ecc.7.25: Eu virei o meu coração para saber, e inquirir, e buscar a sabedoria e a razão, e para saber a impiedade da estulticia e a doidice dos desvarios.
texts.ecc.7.26: E eu achei uma coisa mais amarga do que a morte, a mulher cujo coração são redes e laços, e as suas mãos ataduras: quem fôr bom diante de Deus escapará d’ella, mas o peccador virá a ser preso por ella.
texts.ecc.7.27: Vedes aqui, isto achei, diz o prégador, conferindo uma coisa com a outra para assim achar a razão d’ellas;
texts.ecc.7.28: A qual ainda busca a minha alma, porém ainda não a achei; um homem entre mil achei eu, mas uma mulher entre todas estas não achei.
texts.ecc.7.29: Vedes aqui, que isto tão sómente achei: que Deus fez ao homem recto, porém elles buscaram muitas invenções.
texts.ecc.8.1: Quem é tal como o sabio? e quem sabe a interpretação das coisas? A sabedoria do homem allumia o seu rosto, e a aspereza do seu rosto se muda.
texts.ecc.8.2: Eu digo: Observa o mandamento do rei, porém segundo a palavra do juramento que fizeste a Deus.
texts.ecc.8.3: Não te apresses a sair da presença d’elle, nem persistas em alguma coisa má, porque elle faz tudo o que quer.
texts.ecc.8.4: Onde ha a palavra do rei, ahi está o poder; e quem lhe dirá: Que fazes?
texts.ecc.8.5: Quem guardar o mandamento não experimentará nenhum mal; e o coração do sabio saberá o tempo e o modo.
texts.ecc.8.6: Porque para todo o proposito ha seu tempo e seu modo; porquanto o mal do homem é muito sobre elle.
texts.ecc.8.7: Porque não sabe o que ha de succeder: e, quando haja de succeder, quem lh’o dará a entender?
texts.ecc.8.8: Nenhum homem ha que tenha dominio sobre o espirito, para reter o espirito; nem tão pouco tem elle poder sobre o dia da morte: como tambem nem armas n’esta peleja: nem tão pouco a impiedade livrará aos impios.
texts.ecc.8.9: Tudo isto vi quando appliquei o meu coração a toda a obra que se faz debaixo do sol: tempo ha em que um homem tem dominio sobre outro homem, para desgraça sua.
texts.ecc.8.10: Assim tambem vi os impios sepultados, e os que vinham, e sahiam do logar sancto, que foram esquecidos na cidade em que fizeram bem: tambem isto é vaidade.
texts.ecc.8.11: Porquanto logo se não executa o juizo sobre a má obra, por isso o coração dos filhos dos homens está inteiramente disposto para obrar o mal.
texts.ecc.8.12: Ainda que o peccador faça mal cem vezes, e os dias se lhe prolonguem, comtudo bem sei eu, que bem succede aos que temem a Deus, aos que temerem diante d’elle.
texts.ecc.8.13: Porém ao impio não irá bem, e elle não prolongará os dias; será como a sombra; visto que elle não teme diante de Deus.
texts.ecc.8.14: Ainda ha outra vaidade que se faz sobre a terra: que ha justos a quem succede segundo as obras dos impios, e ha impios a quem succede segundo as obras dos justos. Digo que tambem isto é vaidade.
texts.ecc.8.15: Assim que louvei eu a alegria, porquanto o homem coisa nenhuma melhor tem debaixo do sol do que comer, beber e alegrar-se; porque isso o acompanhará no seu trabalho nos dias da sua vida que Deus lhe dá debaixo do sol.
texts.ecc.8.16: Applicando eu o meu coração a entender a sabedoria, e a ver a occupação que ha sobre a terra; que nem de dia nem de noite vê o homem somno nos seus olhos.
texts.ecc.8.17: Então vi toda a obra de Deus, que o homem não pode alcançar, a obra que se faz debaixo do sol, pela qual trabalha o homem para a buscar, porém não a achará; e, ainda que diga o sabio que a virá a saber, nem por isso a poderá alcançar.
texts.ecc.9.1: Devéras revolvi todas estas coisas no meu coração, para claramente entender tudo isto: que os justos, e os sabios, e as suas obras, estão nas mãos de Deus, como tambem que não conhece o homem nem o amor nem o odio, por tudo o que passa perante a sua face.
texts.ecc.9.2: Tudo succede a uns, como a todos os outros; o mesmo succede ao justo e ao impio; ao bom e ao puro, como ao impuro; assim ao que sacrifica como ao que não sacrifica; assim ao bom como ao peccador; ao que jura como ao que teme o juramento.
texts.ecc.9.3: Este mal ha entre tudo quanto se faz debaixo do sol, que a todos succede o mesmo; e que tambem o coração dos filhos dos homens esteja cheio de maldade, e que haja desvarios no seu coração, na sua vida, e depois se vão aos mortos.
texts.ecc.9.4: Porque para o que acompanha com todos os vivos ha esperança (porque melhor é o cão vivo do que o leão morto).
texts.ecc.9.5: Porque os vivos sabem que hão de morrer, mas os mortos não sabem coisa nenhuma, nem tão pouco teem elles jámais paga, mas a sua memoria ficou entregue ao esquecimento.
texts.ecc.9.6: Até o seu amor, até o seu odio, e até a sua inveja já pereceu, e já não teem parte alguma n’este seculo, em coisa alguma do que se faz debaixo do sol.
texts.ecc.9.7: Vae, pois, come com alegria o teu pão e bebe com bom coração o teu vinho, pois já Deus se agrada das tuas obras.
texts.ecc.9.8: Em todo o tempo sejam alvos os teus vestidos, e nunca falte o oleo sobre a tua cabeça.
texts.ecc.9.9: Goza a vida com a mulher que amas, todos os dias da vida da tua vaidade, os quaes Deus te deu debaixo do sol, todos os dias da tua vaidade: porque esta é a tua porção n’esta vida, e no teu trabalho, em que tu trabalhaste debaixo do sol.
texts.ecc.9.10: Tudo quanto te vier á mão para fazer, faze-o conforme as tuas forças, porque na sepultura, para onde tu vaes, não ha obra, nem industria, nem sciencia, nem sabedoria alguma.
texts.ecc.9.11: Volvi-me, e vi debaixo do sol que não é dos ligeiros a carreira, nem dos valentes a peleja, nem tão pouco dos sabios o pão, nem tão pouco dos prudentes as riquezas, nem tão pouco dos entendidos o favor, mas que o tempo e o acaso lhes succedem a todos.
texts.ecc.9.12: Que tambem o homem não sabe o seu tempo; assim como os peixes que se pescam com a rede maligna, e como os passarinhos que se prendem com o laço, assim se enlaçam tambem os filhos dos homens no mau tempo, quando cae de repente sobre elles.
texts.ecc.9.13: Tambem vi esta sabedoria debaixo do sol, que foi para comigo grande;
texts.ecc.9.14: Houve uma pequena cidade em que havia poucos homens, e veiu contra ella um grande rei, e a cercou e levantou contra ella grandes tranqueiras:
texts.ecc.9.15: E se achou n’ella um sabio pobre, que livrou aquella cidade pela sua sabedoria, e ninguem se lembrava d’aquelle pobre homem.
texts.ecc.9.16: Então disse eu: Melhor é a sabedoria do que a força, ainda que a sabedoria do pobre foi desprezada, e as suas palavras não foram ouvidas.
texts.ecc.9.17: As palavras dos sabios em silencio se devem ouvir, mais do que o clamor do que domina sobre os tolos.
texts.ecc.9.18: Melhor é a sabedoria do que as armas de guerra, porém um só peccador destroe muitos bens.
texts.ecc.10.1: Assim como a mosca morta faz exhalar mau cheiro e evaporar o unguento do perfumador, assim o faz ao famoso em sabedoria e em honra uma pouca de estulticia.
texts.ecc.10.2: O coração do sabio está á sua dextra, mas o coração do tolo está á sua esquerda.
texts.ecc.10.3: E, até quando o tolo vae pelo caminho, falta-lhe o seu entendimento e diz a todos que é tolo.
texts.ecc.10.4: Levantando-se contra ti o espirito do governador, não deixes o teu logar, porque é um remedio que aquieta grandes peccados.
texts.ecc.10.5: Ainda ha um mal que vi debaixo do sol, como o erro que procede de diante do governador.
texts.ecc.10.6: Ao tolo assentam em grandes alturas, mas os ricos estão assentados na baixeza.
texts.ecc.10.7: Vi os servos a cavallo, e os principes que andavam a pé como servos sobre a terra.
texts.ecc.10.8: Quem cavar uma cova, cairá n’ella, e, quem romper um muro, uma cobra o morderá.
texts.ecc.10.9: Quem acarretar pedras, será maltratado por ellas, e o que rachar lenha perigará com ella.
texts.ecc.10.10: Se estiver embotado o ferro, e não se amollar o córte, então se devem pôr mais forças: mas a sabedoria é excellente para dirigir.
texts.ecc.10.11: Se a cobra morder, não estando encantada, então remedio nenhum se espera do encantador, por mais habil que seja.
texts.ecc.10.12: Nas palavras da bocca do sabio ha favor, porém os labios do tolo o devoram.
texts.ecc.10.13: O principio das palavras da sua bocca é a estulticia, e o fim da sua bocca um desvario pessimo.
texts.ecc.10.14: Bem que o tolo multiplique as palavras, não sabe o homem o que ha de ser; e quem lhe fará saber o que será depois d’elle?
texts.ecc.10.15: O trabalho dos tolos a cada um d’elles fatiga, porque não sabem ir á cidade.
texts.ecc.10.16: Ai de ti, ó terra, cujo rei é criança, e cujos principes comem de manhã.
texts.ecc.10.17: Bemaventurada tu, ó terra, cujo rei é filho dos nobres, e cujos principes comem a tempo, para refazerem as forças, e não para bebedice.
texts.ecc.10.18: Pela muita preguiça se enfraquece o tecto, e pela frouxidão das mãos goteja a casa.
texts.ecc.10.19: Para rir se fazem convites, e o vinho alegra a vida, e por tudo o dinheiro responde.
texts.ecc.10.20: Nem ainda no teu pensamento amaldiçoes ao rei, nem tão pouco no mais interior da tua recamara amaldiçoes ao rico: porque as aves dos céus levariam a voz, e os que teem azas dariam noticia da palavra.
texts.ecc.11.1: Lança o teu pão sobre as aguas, porque depois de muitos dias o acharás.
texts.ecc.11.2: Reparte com sete, e ainda até com oito, porque não sabes que mal haverá sobre a terra.
texts.ecc.11.3: Estando as nuvens cheias, vazam a chuva sobre a terra, e caindo a arvore para o sul, ou para o norte, no logar em que a arvore cair ali ficará.
texts.ecc.11.4: Quem observa o vento, nunca semeará, e o que olha para as nuvens nunca segará.
texts.ecc.11.5: Assim como tu não sabes qual o caminho do vento, nem como se formam os ossos no ventre da mulher gravida, assim tu não sabes as obras de Deus, que faz todas as coisas.
texts.ecc.11.6: Pela manhã semeia a tua semente, e á tarde não retires a tua mão, porque tu não sabes qual será recto, se isto, se aquillo, ou se ambas estas coisas egualmente serão boas.
texts.ecc.11.7: Devéras suave é a luz, e agradavel é aos olhos ver o sol.
texts.ecc.11.8: Porém se o homem viver muitos annos, e em todos elles se alegrar, tambem se deve lembrar dos dias das trevas, porque hão de ser muitos, e tudo quanto succedeu é vaidade.
texts.ecc.11.9: Alegra-te, mancebo, na tua mocidade, e recreie-se o teu coração nos dias da tua mocidade, e anda pelos caminhos do teu coração, e pela vista dos teus olhos: sabe, porém, que por todas estas coisas te trará Deus a juizo.
texts.ecc.11.10: Afasta pois a ira do teu coração, e remove da tua carne o mal, porque a adolescencia e a juventude são vaidade.
texts.ecc.12.1: Lembra-te do teu Creador nos dias da tua mocidade, antes que venham os maus dias, e cheguem os annos dos quaes venhas a dizer: Não tenho n’elles contentamento:
texts.ecc.12.2: Antes que se escureçam o sol, e a luz, e a lua, e as estrellas, e tornem a vir as nuvens depois da chuva;
texts.ecc.12.3: No dia em que tremerem os guardas da casa, e se encurvarem os fortes varões, e cessarem os moedores, por já serem poucos, e se escurecerem os que olham pelas janellas;
texts.ecc.12.4: E as duas portas da rua se fecharem por causa do baixo ruido da moedura, e se levantar á voz das aves, e todas as vozes do canto se encurvarem:
texts.ecc.12.5: Como tambem quando temerem os logares altos, e houver espantos no caminho, e florescer a amendoeira, e o gafanhoto o carregar, e perecer o appetite, porque o homem se vae á sua eterna casa, e os pranteadores andarão rodeando pela praça.
texts.ecc.12.6: Antes que se quebre a cadeia de prata, e se despedace o copo d’oiro, e se despedace o cantaro junto á fonte, e se despedace a roda junto ao poço,
texts.ecc.12.7: E o pó voltar á terra, como o era, e o espirito voltar a Deus, que o deu.
texts.ecc.12.8: Vaidade de vaidade, diz o prégador, tudo é vaidade.
texts.ecc.12.9: E, quanto mais o prégador foi sabio, tanto mais sabedoria ao povo ensinou, e attentou, e esquadrinhou, e compoz muitos proverbios.
texts.ecc.12.10: Procurou o prégador achar palavras agradaveis; e o escripto é a rectidão, palavras de verdade.
texts.ecc.12.11: As palavras dos sabios são como aguilhões, e como pregos, bem affixados pelos mestres das congregações, que nos foram dados pelo unico Pastor.
texts.ecc.12.12: E, de mais d’isto, filho meu, attenta: não ha limite para fazer livros, e o muito estudar enfado é da carne.
texts.ecc.12.13: De tudo o que se tem ouvido, o fim da coisa é: Teme a Deus, e guarda os seus mandamentos; porque isto é o dever de todo o homem.
texts.ecc.12.14: Porque Deus ha de trazer a juizo toda a obra, e até tudo o que está encoberto, quer seja bom quer seja mau.

texts.ecc.1.1: The words of the preacher, the son of David, king of Jerusalem.
texts.ecc.1.2: Vanity of vanities, saith the preacher, vanity of vanities; all is vanity.
texts.ecc.1.3: What profit hath a man of all his labor, which he taketh under the sun?
texts.ecc.1.4: One generation passeth away, and another generation cometh: but the earth abideth for ever.
texts.ecc.1.5: The sun also riseth, and the sun goeth down, and hasteth to his place where he arose.
texts.ecc.1.6: The wind goeth towards the south, and turneth about to the north; it whirleth about continually, and the wind returneth again according to its circuits.
texts.ecc.1.7: All the rivers run into the sea; yet the sea is not full; to the place from whence the rivers come, thither they return again.
texts.ecc.1.8: All things are full of labor; man cannot utter it: the eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.
texts.ecc.1.9: The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be; and that which is done is that which shall be done: and there is no new thing under the sun.
texts.ecc.1.10: Is there any thing of which it may be said, See, this is new? it hath been already of old time, which was before us.
texts.ecc.1.11: There is no remembrance of former things; neither shall there be any remembrance of things that are to come with those that shall come after.
texts.ecc.1.12: I the preacher was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
texts.ecc.1.13: And I gave my heart to seek and search out by wisdom concerning all things that are done under heaven: this grievous labor hath God given to the sons of man to be exercised with it.
texts.ecc.1.14: I have seen all the works that are done under the sun; and behold, all is vanity and vexation of spirit.
texts.ecc.1.15: That which is crooked cannot be made straight: and that which is wanting cannot be numbered.
texts.ecc.1.16: I communed with my own heart, saying, Lo, I have come to great estate, and have gained more wisdom than all they that have been before me in Jerusalem: and my heart had great experience of wisdom and knowledge.
texts.ecc.1.17: And I gave my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly: I perceived that this also is vexation of spirit.
texts.ecc.1.18: For in much wisdom is much grief: and he that increaseth knowledge increaseth sorrow.
texts.ecc.2.1: I said in my heart, Come now, I will prove thee with mirth, therefore enjoy pleasure: and behold, this also is vanity.
texts.ecc.2.2: I said of laughter, It is mad: and of mirth, What doeth it?
texts.ecc.2.3: I sought in my heart, to give myself to wine, yet acquainting my heart with wisdom; and to lay hold on folly, till I might see what was that good for the sons of men, which they should do under the heaven all the days of their life.
texts.ecc.2.4: I made me great works; I built me houses; I planted me vineyards:
texts.ecc.2.5: I made me gardens and orchards, and I planted trees in them of all kind of fruits:
texts.ecc.2.6: I made me pools of water, to water with them the wood that bringeth forth trees:
texts.ecc.2.7: I procured me servants and maidens, and had servants born in my house; also I had great possessions of great and small cattle above all that were in Jerusalem before me:
texts.ecc.2.8: I gathered me also silver and gold, and the peculiar treasure of kings, and of the provinces: I procured me men-singers and women-singers, and the delights of the sons of men, as musical instruments, and of all sorts.
texts.ecc.2.9: So I was great, and increased more than all that were before me in Jerusalem: also my wisdom remained with me.
texts.ecc.2.10: And whatever my eyes desired I kept not from them, I withheld not my heart from any joy; for my heart rejoiced in all my labor: and this was my portion of all my labor.
texts.ecc.2.11: Then I looked on all the works that my hands had wrought, and on the labor that I had labored to do: and behold, all was vanity and vexation of spirit, and there was no profit under the sun.
texts.ecc.2.12: And I turned myself to behold wisdom, and madness, and folly: for what can the man do that cometh after the king? even that which hath been already done.
texts.ecc.2.13: Then I saw that wisdom excelleth folly, as far as light excelleth darkness.
texts.ecc.2.14: The wise man's eyes are in his head; but the fool walketh in darkness: and I myself perceived also that one event happeneth to them all.
texts.ecc.2.15: Then said I in my heart, As it happeneth to the fool, so it happeneth even to me; and why was I then more wise? Then I said in my heart, that this also is vanity.
texts.ecc.2.16: For there is no remembrance of the wise more than of the fool for ever; seeing that which now is in the days to come shall all be forgotten. And how dieth the wise man? as the fool.
texts.ecc.2.17: Therefore I hated life; because the work that is wrought under the sun is grievous to me: for all is vanity and vexation of spirit.
texts.ecc.2.18: Yes, I hated all my labor which I had taken under the sun: because I should leave it to the man that shall be after me.
texts.ecc.2.19: And who knoweth whether he shall be a wise man or a fool? yet shall he have rule over all my labor in which I have labored, and in which I have showed myself wise under the sun. This is also vanity.
texts.ecc.2.20: Therefore I went about to cause my heart to despair of all the labor which I took under the sun.
texts.ecc.2.21: For there is a man whose labor is in wisdom, and in knowledge, and in equity; yet to a man that hath not labored in it, shall he leave it for his portion. This also is vanity and a great evil.
texts.ecc.2.22: For what hath man of all his labor, and of the vexation of his heart, in which he hath labored under the sun?
texts.ecc.2.23: For all his days are sorrows, and his labor grief; yes, his heart taketh not rest in the night. This is also vanity.
texts.ecc.2.24: There is nothing better for a man than that he should eat and drink, and that he should make his soul enjoy good in his labor. This also I saw, that it was from the hand of God.
texts.ecc.2.25: For who can eat, or who else can hasten to it more than I?
texts.ecc.2.26: For God giveth to a man who is good in his sight, wisdom, and knowledge, and joy: but to the sinner he giveth toil, to gather, and to amass, that he may give to him that is good before God. This also is vanity and vexation of spirit.
texts.ecc.3.1: To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven:
texts.ecc.3.2: A time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pluck up that which is planted;
texts.ecc.3.3: A time to kill, and a time to heal; a time to break down, and a time to build up;
texts.ecc.3.4: A time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;
texts.ecc.3.5: A time to cast away stones, and a time to gather stones; a time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing;
texts.ecc.3.6: A time to get, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to cast away;
texts.ecc.3.7: A time to rend, and a time to sew; a time to keep silence, and a time to speak;
texts.ecc.3.8: A time to love, and a time to hate; a time of war, and a time of peace.
texts.ecc.3.9: What profit hath he that worketh in that in which he laboreth?
texts.ecc.3.10: I have seen the labor, which God hath given to the sons of men to be exercised in it.
texts.ecc.3.11: He hath made every thing beautiful in its time: also he hath set the world in their heart, so that no man can find out the work that God maketh from the beginning to the end.
texts.ecc.3.12: I know that there is no good in them, but for a man to rejoice, and to do good in his life.
texts.ecc.3.13: And also that every man should eat and drink, and enjoy the good of all his labor, it is the gift of God.
texts.ecc.3.14: I know that, whatever God doeth, it shall be for ever: nothing can be added to it, nor any thing taken from it: and God doeth it, that men should fear before him.
texts.ecc.3.15: That which hath been is now; and that which is to be hath already been; and God requireth that which is past.
texts.ecc.3.16: And moreover I saw under the sun the place of judgment, that wickedness was there; and the place of righteousness, that iniquity was there.
texts.ecc.3.17: I said in my heart, God will judge the righteous and the wicked: for there is a time there for every purpose and for every work.
texts.ecc.3.18: I said in my heart concerning the state of the sons of men, that God might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts.
texts.ecc.3.19: For that which befalleth the sons of men befalleth beasts; even one thing befalleth them: as the one dieth, so dieth the other; yes, they have all one breath; so that a man hath no pre-eminence above a beast: for all is vanity.
texts.ecc.3.20: All go to one place; all are of the dust, and all turn to dust again.
texts.ecc.3.21: Who knoweth the spirit of man that goeth upward, and the spirit of the beast that goeth downward to the earth?
texts.ecc.3.22: Wherefore I perceive that there is nothing better, than that a man should rejoice in his own works; for that is his portion: for who shall bring him to see what shall be after him?
texts.ecc.4.1: So I returned, and considered all the oppressions that are done under the sun: and behold the tears of such as were oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors there was power; but they had no comforter.
texts.ecc.4.2: Wherefore I praised the dead who are already dead more than the living who are yet alive.
texts.ecc.4.3: Yes, better is he than both they, who hath not yet been, who hath not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.
texts.ecc.4.4: Again, I considered all labor, and every right work, that for this a man is envied by his neighbor. This is also vanity and vexation of spirit.
texts.ecc.4.5: The fool foldeth his hands together, and eateth his own flesh.
texts.ecc.4.6: Better is a handful with quietness, than both the hands full with toil and vexation of spirit.
texts.ecc.4.7: Then I returned, and I saw vanity under the sun.
texts.ecc.4.8: There is one alone, and there is not a second; yes, he hath neither child nor brother: yet is there no end of all his labor; neither is his eye satisfied with riches; neither saith he, For whom do I labor, and bereave my soul of good? This is also vanity, yes, it is a grievous labor.
texts.ecc.4.9: Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labor.
texts.ecc.4.10: For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him that is alone when he falleth; for he hath not another to help him to rise.
texts.ecc.4.11: Again, if two lie together, then they have heat: but how can one be warm alone?
texts.ecc.4.12: And if one prevaileth against him, two shall withstand him; and a three-fold cord is not quickly broken.
texts.ecc.4.13: Better is a poor and a wise child, than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished.
texts.ecc.4.14: For out of prison he cometh to reign; whereas also he that is born in his kingdom becometh poor.
texts.ecc.4.15: I considered all the living who walk under the sun, with the second child that shall stand up in his stead.
texts.ecc.4.16: There is no end of all the people, even of all that have been before them: they also that come after shall not rejoice in him. Surely this also is vanity and vexation of spirit.
texts.ecc.5.1: Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God, and be more ready to hear, than to give the sacrifice of fools: for they consider not that they do evil.
texts.ecc.5.2: Be not rash with thy mouth, and let not thy heart be hasty to utter any thing before God: for God is in heaven, and thou upon earth: therefore let thy words be few.
texts.ecc.5.3: For a dream cometh through the multitude of business; and a fool's voice is known by a multitude of words.
texts.ecc.5.4: When thou vowest a vow to God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed.
texts.ecc.5.5: Better is it that thou shouldst not vow, than that thou shouldst vow and not pay.
texts.ecc.5.6: Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin; neither say thou before the angel, that it was an error: why should God be angry at thy voice, and destroy the work of thy hands?
texts.ecc.5.7: For in the multitude of dreams and many words there are also divers vanities: but fear thou God.
texts.ecc.5.8: If thou seest the oppression of the poor, and violent perversion of judgment and justice in a province, wonder not at the matter: for he that is higher than the highest regardeth; and there are higher than they.
texts.ecc.5.9: Moreover, the profit of the earth is for all: the king himself is served by the field.
texts.ecc.5.10: He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he that loveth abundance with increase: this is also vanity.
texts.ecc.5.11: When goods increase, they are increased that eat them: and what good is there to the owners of them, saving the beholding of them with their eyes?
texts.ecc.5.12: The sleep of a laboring man is sweet, whether he eateth little or much: but the abundance of the rich will not suffer him to sleep.
texts.ecc.5.13: There is a grievous evil which I have seen under the sun, namely, riches kept for the owners of them to their hurt.
texts.ecc.5.14: But those riches perish by evil labor: and he begetteth a son, and there is nothing in his hand.
texts.ecc.5.15: As he came into the world, naked shall he return to go as he came, and shall take nothing of his labor, which he may carry away in his hand.
texts.ecc.5.16: And this also is a grievous evil, that in all points as he came, so shall he go: and what profit hath he that hath labored for the wind?
texts.ecc.5.17: All his days also he eateth in darkness, and he hath much sorrow and wrath with his sickness.
texts.ecc.5.18: Behold that which I have seen: it is good and comely for one to eat and to drink, and to enjoy the good of all his labor that he taketh under the sun all the days of his life, which God giveth him: for it is his portion.
texts.ecc.5.19: Every man also to whom God hath given riches and wealth, and hath given him power to eat of it, and to take his portion, and to rejoice in his labor; this is the gift of God.
texts.ecc.5.20: For he shall not much remember the days of his life; because God answereth him in the joy of his heart.
texts.ecc.6.1: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it is common among men:
texts.ecc.6.2: A man to whom God hath given riches, wealth, and honor, so that he wanteth nothing for his soul of all that he desireth, yet God giveth him not power to eat of it, but a stranger eateth it: this is vanity, and it is an evil disease.
texts.ecc.6.3: If a man begetteth a hundred children, and liveth many years, so that the days of his years are many, and his soul is not filled with good, and also that he hath no burial; I say, that an untimely birth is better than he.
texts.ecc.6.4: For he cometh with vanity, and departeth in darkness, and his name shall be covered with darkness.
texts.ecc.6.5: Moreover he hath not seen the sun, nor known any thing: this hath more rest than the other.
texts.ecc.6.6: Yes, though he liveth a thousand years twice told, yet hath he seen no good: do not all go to one place?
texts.ecc.6.7: All the labor of man is for his mouth, and yet the appetite is not filled.
texts.ecc.6.8: For what hath the wise more than the fool? what hath the poor, that knoweth to walk before the living?
texts.ecc.6.9: Better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the desire: this is also vanity and vexation of spirit.
texts.ecc.6.10: That which hath been is named already, and it is known that it is man: neither may he contend with him that is mightier than he.
texts.ecc.6.11: Seeing there are many things that increase vanity, what is man the better?
texts.ecc.6.12: For who knoweth what is good for man in this life, all the days of his vain life which he spendeth as a shadow? for who can tell a man what shall be after him under the sun?
texts.ecc.7.1: A good name is better than precious ointment; and the day of death than the day of one's birth.
texts.ecc.7.2: It is better to go to the house of mourning, than to go to the house of feasting: for that is the end of all men; and the living will lay it to his heart.
texts.ecc.7.3: Sorrow is better than laughter: for by the sadness of the countenance the heart is made better.
texts.ecc.7.4: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth.
texts.ecc.7.5: It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise, than for a man to hear the song of fools.
texts.ecc.7.6: For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of the fool: this also is vanity.
texts.ecc.7.7: Surely oppression maketh a wise man mad; and a gift destroyeth the heart.
texts.ecc.7.8: Better is the end of a thing than its beginning: and the patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.
texts.ecc.7.9: Be not hasty in thy spirit to be angry: for anger resteth in the bosom of fools.
texts.ecc.7.10: Say not thou, What is the cause that the former days were better than these? for thou dost not inquire wisely concerning this.
texts.ecc.7.11: Wisdom is good with an inheritance: and by it there is profit to them that see the sun.
texts.ecc.7.12: For wisdom is a defense, and money is a defense: but the excellence of knowledge is, that wisdom giveth life to them that have it.
texts.ecc.7.13: Consider the work of God: for who can make that straight, which he hath made crooked?
texts.ecc.7.14: In the day of prosperity be joyful, but in the day of adversity consider: God also hath set the one over against the other, to the end that man should find nothing after him.
texts.ecc.7.15: All things have I seen in the days of my vanity: there is a just man that perisheth in his righteousness, and there is a wicked man that prolongeth his life in his wickedness.
texts.ecc.7.16: Be not righteous over much; neither make thyself over wise: why shouldst thou destroy thyself?
texts.ecc.7.17: Be not over much wicked, neither be thou foolish: why shouldst thou die before thy time?
texts.ecc.7.18: It is good that thou shouldst take hold of this; yes, also from this withdraw not thy hand: for he that feareth God shall escape from them all.
texts.ecc.7.19: Wisdom strengtheneth the wise more than ten mighty men who are in the city.
texts.ecc.7.20: For there is not a just man upon earth, that doeth good, and sinneth not.
texts.ecc.7.21: Also take no heed to all words that are spoken; lest thou hear thy servant curse thee:
texts.ecc.7.22: For often also thy own heart knoweth that thou thyself likewise hast cursed others.
texts.ecc.7.23: All this have I proved by wisdom: I said, I will be wise; but it was far from me.
texts.ecc.7.24: That which is far off, and exceedingly deep, who can find it out?
texts.ecc.7.25: I applied my heart to know, and to search, and to seek out wisdom, and the reason of things, and to know the wickedness of folly, even of foolishness and madness:
texts.ecc.7.26: And I find more bitter than death the woman whose heart is snares and nets, and her hands as bands: whoever pleaseth God shall escape from her; but the sinner shall be taken by her.
texts.ecc.7.27: Behold, this have I found, saith the preacher, counting one by one, to find out the account:
texts.ecc.7.28: Which yet my soul seeketh, but I find not: one man among a thousand have I found; but a woman among all those have I not found.
texts.ecc.7.29: Lo, this only have I found, that God hath made man upright; but they have sought out many inventions.
texts.ecc.8.1: Who is as the wise man? and who knoweth the interpretation of a thing? a man's wisdom maketh his face to shine, and the boldness of his face shall be changed.
texts.ecc.8.2: I counsel thee to keep the king's commandment, and that in regard of the oath of God.
texts.ecc.8.3: Be not hasty to go out of his sight: stand not in an evil thing; for he doeth whatever pleaseth him.
texts.ecc.8.4: Where the word of a king is, there is power: and who may say to him, what doest thou?
texts.ecc.8.5: He who keepeth the commandment shall feel no evil thing: and a wise man's heart discerneth both time and judgment.
texts.ecc.8.6: Because to every purpose there is time and judgment, therefore the misery of man is great upon him.
texts.ecc.8.7: For he knoweth not that which shall be: for who can tell him when it shall be?
texts.ecc.8.8: There is no man that hath power over the spirit to retain the spirit; neither hath he power in the day of death: and there is no discharge in that war; neither shall wickedness deliver those that are given to it.
texts.ecc.8.9: All this have I seen, and applied my heart to every work that is done under the sun: there is a time in which one man ruleth over another to his own hurt.
texts.ecc.8.10: And so I saw the wicked buried, who had come and gone from the place of the holy, and they were forgotten in the city where they had so done: this is also vanity.
texts.ecc.8.11: Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.
texts.ecc.8.12: Though a sinner doeth evil a hundred times, and his days are prolonged, yet surely I know that it will be well with them that fear God, who fear before him:
texts.ecc.8.13: But it will not be well with the wicked, neither will he prolong his days, which are as a shadow; because he feareth not before God.
texts.ecc.8.14: There is a vanity which is done upon the earth; that there are just men, to whom it happeneth according to the work of the wicked; again, there are wicked men, to whom it happeneth according to the work of the righteous: I said that this also is vanity.
texts.ecc.8.15: Then I commended mirth, because a man hath no better thing under the sun, than to eat, and to drink, and to be merry: for that shall abide with him of his labor the days of his life, which God giveth him under the sun.
texts.ecc.8.16: When I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to see the business that is done upon the earth: (for also there is that neither day nor night seeth sleep with his eyes:)
texts.ecc.8.17: Then I beheld all the work of God, that a man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun: because though a man may labor to seek it out, yet he shall not find it; yes further; though a wise man thinketh to know it, yet shall he not be able to find it.
texts.ecc.9.1: For all this I considered in my heart even to declare all this, that the righteous, and the wise, and their works, are in the hand of God: no man knoweth either love or hatred by all that is before them.
texts.ecc.9.2: All things come alike to all: there is one event to the righteous, and to the wicked; to the good and to the clean, and to the unclean; to him that sacrificeth, and to him that sacrificeth not: as is the good, so is the sinner; and he that sweareth, as he that feareth an oath.
texts.ecc.9.3: This is an evil among all things that are done under the sun, that there is one event to all: yes, also the heart of the sons of men is full of evil, and madness is in their heart while they live, and after that they go to the dead.
texts.ecc.9.4: For to him that is joined to all the living there is hope: for a living dog is better than a dead lion.
texts.ecc.9.5: For the living know that they shall die: but the dead know not any thing, neither have they any more a reward; for the memory of them is forgotten.
texts.ecc.9.6: Also their love, and their hatred, and their envy, hath now perished; neither have they any more a portion for ever in any thing that is done under the sun.
texts.ecc.9.7: Go thy way, eat thy bread with joy, and drink thy wine with a merry heart; for God now accepteth thy works.
texts.ecc.9.8: Let thy garments be always white; and let thy head lack no ointment.
texts.ecc.9.9: Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, which he hath given thee under the sun, all the days of thy vanity: for that is thy portion in this life, and in thy labor which thou takest under the sun.
texts.ecc.9.10: Whatever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might; for there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in the grave, whither thou goest.
texts.ecc.9.11: I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favor to men of skill; but time and chance happeneth to them all.
texts.ecc.9.12: For man also knoweth not his time: as the fishes that are taken in an evil net, and as the birds that are caught in the snare; so are the sons of men snared in an evil time, when it falleth suddenly upon them.
texts.ecc.9.13: This wisdom have I seen also under the sun, and it seemed to me great:
texts.ecc.9.14: There was a little city, and few men within it; and there came a great king against it, and besieged it, and built great bulwarks against it:
texts.ecc.9.15: Now there was found in it a poor wise man, and he by his wisdom delivered the city; yet no man remembered that same poor man.
texts.ecc.9.16: Then said I, wisdom is better than strength: nevertheless the poor man's wisdom is despised, and his words are not heard.
texts.ecc.9.17: The words of wise men are heard in quiet more than the cry of him that ruleth among fools.
texts.ecc.9.18: Wisdom is better than weapons of war: but one sinner destroyeth much good.
texts.ecc.10.1: Dead flies cause the ointment of the apothecary to send forth an offensive odor: so doth a little folly him that is in reputation for wisdom and honor.
texts.ecc.10.2: A wise man's heart is at his right hand; but a fool's heart is at his left.
texts.ecc.10.3: Also, when he that is a fool walketh by the way, his wisdom faileth him, and he saith to every one that he is a fool.
texts.ecc.10.4: If the spirit of the ruler riseth against thee, leave not thy place; for yielding pacifieth great offenses.
texts.ecc.10.5: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, as an error which proceedeth from the ruler:
texts.ecc.10.6: Folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in low place.
texts.ecc.10.7: I have seen servants upon horses, and princes walking as servants upon the earth.
texts.ecc.10.8: He that diggeth a pit shall fall into it; and whoever breaketh a hedge, a serpent shall bite him.
texts.ecc.10.9: Whoever removeth stones shall be hurt by them; and he that cleaveth wood shall be endangered by it.
texts.ecc.10.10: If the iron is blunt, and he doth not whet the edge, then must he use more strength: but wisdom is profitable to direct.
texts.ecc.10.11: Surely the serpent will bite without enchantment; and a babbler is no better.
texts.ecc.10.12: The words of a wise man's mouth are gracious; but the lips of a fool will swallow up himself.
texts.ecc.10.13: The beginning of the words of his mouth is foolishness: and the end of his talk is mischievous madness.
texts.ecc.10.14: A fool also is full of words: a man cannot tell what shall be; and what shall be after him, who can tell him?
texts.ecc.10.15: The labor of the foolish wearieth every one of them, because he knoweth not how to go to the city.
texts.ecc.10.16: Woe to thee, O land, when thy king is a child, and thy princes eat in the morning!
texts.ecc.10.17: Blessed art thou, O land, when thy king is the son of nobles, and thy princes eat in due season, for strength, and not for drunkenness!
texts.ecc.10.18: By much slothfulness the building decayeth; and through idleness of the hands the house droppeth through.
texts.ecc.10.19: A feast is made for laughter, and wine maketh merry: but money answereth all things.
texts.ecc.10.20: Curse not the king, no not in thy thought; and curse not the rich in thy bed-chamber: for a bird of the air will carry the voice, and that which hath wings will tell the matter.
texts.ecc.11.1: Cast thy bread upon the waters: for thou shalt find it after many days.
texts.ecc.11.2: Give a portion to seven, and also to eight; for thou knowest not what evil shall be upon the earth.
texts.ecc.11.3: If the clouds are full of rain, they empty themselves upon the earth: and if the tree falleth towards the south, or towards the north, in the place where the tree falleth, there it shall be.
texts.ecc.11.4: He that observeth the wind shall not sow; and he that regardeth the clouds shall not reap.
texts.ecc.11.5: As thou knowest not what is the way of the spirit, nor the structure of the parts of conception in her that is with child: even so thou knowest not the works of God who maketh all.
texts.ecc.11.6: In the morning sow thy seed, and in the evening withhold not thy hand: for thou knowest not whether shall prosper, either this or that, or whether they both shall be alike good.
texts.ecc.11.7: Truly the light is sweet, and a pleasant thing it is for the eyes to behold the sun:
texts.ecc.11.8: But if a man shall live many years, and rejoice in them all; yet let him remember the days of darkness; for they shall be many. All that cometh is vanity.
texts.ecc.11.9: Rejoice, O young man, in thy youth; and let thy heart cheer thee in the days of thy youth, and walk in the ways of thy heart, and in the sight of thy eyes: but know thou, that for all these things God will bring thee into judgment.
texts.ecc.11.10: Therefore remove sorrow from thy heart, and put away evil from thy flesh: for childhood and youth are vanity.
texts.ecc.12.1: Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth, while the evil days come not, nor the years draw nigh, when thou shalt say, I have no pleasure in them;
texts.ecc.12.2: While the sun, or the light, or the moon, or the stars, are not darkened, nor the clouds return after the rain:
texts.ecc.12.3: In the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those that look out of the windows shall be darkened,
texts.ecc.12.4: And the doors shall be shut in the streets, when the sound of the grinding shall be low, and he shall rise up at the voice of the bird, and all the daughters of music shall be brought low.
texts.ecc.12.5: Also when they shall be afraid of that which is high, and fears shall be in the way, and the almond tree shall flourish, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail: because man goeth to his long home, and the mourners go about the streets:
texts.ecc.12.6: Or ever the silver cord shall be loosed, or the golden bowl be broken, or the pitcher be broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern.
texts.ecc.12.7: Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return to God who gave it.
texts.ecc.12.8: Vanity of vanities saith the preacher; all is vanity.
texts.ecc.12.9: And moreover, because the preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge: yes, he gave good heed, and sought out, and set in order many proverbs.
texts.ecc.12.10: The preacher sought to find out acceptable words: and that which was written was upright, even words of truth.
texts.ecc.12.11: The words of the wise are as goads, and as nails fastened by the masters of assemblies, which are given from one shepherd.
texts.ecc.12.12: And further, by these, my son, be admonished: of making many books there is no end; and much study is a weariness of the flesh.
texts.ecc.12.13: Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.
texts.ecc.12.14: For God will bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it is good, or whether it is evil.

texts.ecc.1.1: The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem.
texts.ecc.1.2: Vanity of vanities, saith the Preacher, vanity of vanities! all is vanity.
texts.ecc.1.3: What profit hath man of all his labour wherewith he laboureth under the sun?
texts.ecc.1.4: [One] generation passeth away, and [another] generation cometh, but the earth standeth for ever.
texts.ecc.1.5: The sun also riseth, and the sun goeth down, and hasteth to its place where it ariseth.
texts.ecc.1.6: The wind goeth towards the south, and turneth about towards the north: it turneth about continually, and the wind returneth again to its circuits.
texts.ecc.1.7: All the rivers run into the sea, yet the sea is not full: unto the place whither the rivers go, thither they go again.
texts.ecc.1.8: All things are full of toil; none can express it. The eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.
texts.ecc.1.9: That which hath been is that which shall be; and that which hath been done is that which will be done: and there is nothing new under the sun.
texts.ecc.1.10: Is there a thing whereof it may be said, See, this is new? It hath been already in the ages which were before us.
texts.ecc.1.11: There is no remembrance of former things; neither shall there be remembrance of things that are to come with those who shall live afterwards.
texts.ecc.1.12: I, the Preacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
texts.ecc.1.13: And I applied my heart to seek and search out by wisdom concerning all that is done under the heavens: this grievous occupation hath God given to the children of men to weary themselves therewith.
texts.ecc.1.14: I have seen all the works that are done under the sun, and behold, all is vanity and pursuit of the wind.
texts.ecc.1.15: That which is crooked cannot be made straight; and that which is wanting cannot be numbered.
texts.ecc.1.16: I communed with mine own heart, saying, Lo, I have become great and have acquired wisdom more than all they that have been before me over Jerusalem; and my heart hath seen much of wisdom and knowledge.
texts.ecc.1.17: And I applied my heart to the knowledge of wisdom, and to the knowledge of madness and folly: I perceived that this also is a striving after the wind.
texts.ecc.1.18: For in much wisdom is much vexation, and he that increaseth knowledge increaseth sorrow.
texts.ecc.2.1: I said in my heart, Come now, I will try thee with mirth, therefore enjoy pleasure. But behold, this also is vanity.
texts.ecc.2.2: I said of laughter, Madness! and of mirth, What availeth it?
texts.ecc.2.3: I searched in my heart how to cherish my flesh with wine, while practising my heart with wisdom; and how to lay hold on folly, till I should see what was that good for the children of men which they should do under the heavens all the days of their life.
texts.ecc.2.4: I made me great works; I builded me houses; I planted me vineyards;
texts.ecc.2.5: I made me gardens and parks, and I planted trees in them of every kind of fruit;
texts.ecc.2.6: I made me ponds of water, to water therewith the wood, where the trees are reared.
texts.ecc.2.7: I acquired servants and maidens, and had servants born in my house; also I had great possessions of herds and flocks, above all that had been in Jerusalem before me.
texts.ecc.2.8: I gathered me also silver and gold, and the peculiar treasure of kings and of the provinces; I got me men-singers and women-singers, and the delights of the children of men, a wife and concubines.
texts.ecc.2.9: And I became great, and increased more than all that had been before me in Jerusalem: also my wisdom remained with me.
texts.ecc.2.10: And whatsoever mine eyes desired I kept not from them: I withheld not my heart from any joy; for my heart rejoiced in all my labour, and this was my portion from all my labour.
texts.ecc.2.11: Then I looked on all the works that my hands had wrought, and on the labour that it had cost me to do [them]; and behold, all was vanity and pursuit of the wind, and there was no profit under the sun.
texts.ecc.2.12: And I turned myself to behold wisdom, and madness, and folly; for what shall the man [do] that cometh after the king? -- that which hath already been done.
texts.ecc.2.13: And I saw that wisdom excelleth folly, as light excelleth darkness.
texts.ecc.2.14: The wise man's eyes are in his head, and the fool walketh in darkness; but I myself also perceived that one event happeneth to them all.
texts.ecc.2.15: And I said in my heart, As it happeneth to the fool so will it happen even to me; and why was I then so wise? Then I said in my heart that this also is vanity.
texts.ecc.2.16: For there shall be no remembrance of the wise more than of the fool for ever; because everything is already forgotten in the days which come. And how dieth the wise even as the fool?
texts.ecc.2.17: And I hated life; for the work that is wrought under the sun was grievous unto me; for all is vanity and pursuit of the wind.
texts.ecc.2.18: And I hated all my labour wherewith I had been toiling under the sun, because I should leave it unto the man that shall be after me.
texts.ecc.2.19: And who knoweth whether he will be a wise [man] or a fool? yet shall he have rule over all my labour at which I have laboured, and wherein I have been wise under the sun. This also is vanity.
texts.ecc.2.20: Then I went about to cause my heart to despair of all the labour wherewith I had laboured under the sun.
texts.ecc.2.21: For there is a man whose labour hath been with wisdom, and with knowledge, and with skill, and who leaveth it to a man that hath not laboured therein, to be his portion. This also is vanity and a great evil.
texts.ecc.2.22: For what will man have of all his labour and of the striving of his heart, wherewith he hath wearied himself under the sun?
texts.ecc.2.23: For all his days are sorrows, and his travail vexation: even in the night his heart taketh no rest. This also is vanity.
texts.ecc.2.24: There is nothing good for man, but that he should eat and drink, and that he should make his soul enjoy good in his labour. This also I saw, that it was from the hand of God.
texts.ecc.2.25: For who can eat, or who be eager, more than I?
texts.ecc.2.26: For he giveth to a man that is good in his sight wisdom, and knowledge, and joy; but to the sinner he giveth travail to gather and to heap up, that he may give to him that is good in God's sight. This also is vanity and pursuit of the wind.
texts.ecc.3.1: To everything there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heavens:
texts.ecc.3.2: A time to be born, and a time to die; A time to plant, and a time to pluck up that which is planted;
texts.ecc.3.3: A time to kill, and a time to heal; A time to break down, and a time to build up;
texts.ecc.3.4: A time to weep, and a time to laugh; A time to mourn, and a time to dance;
texts.ecc.3.5: A time to cast away stones, and a time to gather stones together; A time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing;
texts.ecc.3.6: A time to seek, and a time to lose; A time to keep, and a time to cast away;
texts.ecc.3.7: A time to rend, and a time to sew; A time to keep silence, and a time to speak;
texts.ecc.3.8: A time to love, and a time to hate; A time of war, and a time of peace.
texts.ecc.3.9: What profit hath he that worketh from that wherein he laboureth?
texts.ecc.3.10: I have seen the travail that God hath given to the sons of men to toil in.
texts.ecc.3.11: He hath made everything beautiful in its time; also he hath set the world in their heart, so that man findeth not out from the beginning to the end the work that God doeth.
texts.ecc.3.12: I know that there is nothing good for them but to rejoice and to do well in their life;
texts.ecc.3.13: yea also that every man should eat and drink, and enjoy good in all his labour, it is the gift of God.
texts.ecc.3.14: I know that whatever God doeth, it shall be for ever; there is nothing to be added to it, nor anything to be taken from it; and God doeth [it], that [men] should fear before him.
texts.ecc.3.15: That which is was long ago, and that which is to be hath already been; and God bringeth back again that which is past.
texts.ecc.3.16: And moreover I saw under the sun, that in the place of judgment, wickedness was there; and in the place of righteousness, wickedness was there.
texts.ecc.3.17: I said in my heart, God will judge the righteous and the wicked; for there is a time there for every purpose and for every work.
texts.ecc.3.18: I said in my heart, It is thus with the children of men, that God may prove them, and that they should see that they themselves are but beasts.
texts.ecc.3.19: For what befalleth the children of men befalleth beasts; even one thing befalleth them: as the one dieth, so dieth the other, and they have all one breath; and man hath no pre-eminence above the beast: for all is vanity.
texts.ecc.3.20: All go unto one place: all are of the dust, and all return to dust.
texts.ecc.3.21: Who knoweth the spirit of the children of men? Doth it go upwards? and the spirit of the beasts, doth it go downwards to the earth?
texts.ecc.3.22: And I have seen that there is nothing better than that man should rejoice in his own works; for that is his portion; for who shall bring him to see what shall be after him?
texts.ecc.4.1: And I returned and saw all the oppressions that are done under the sun: and behold, the tears of the oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors was power, and they had no comforter.
texts.ecc.4.2: Then I praised the dead who are already dead more than the living who are yet alive;
texts.ecc.4.3: and more fortunate than both is he who hath not yet been, who hath not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.
texts.ecc.4.4: And I saw all labour, and all success of work, that it is man's jealousy of his neighbour. This also is vanity and pursuit of the wind.
texts.ecc.4.5: The fool foldeth his hands together, and eateth his own flesh.
texts.ecc.4.6: Better is a handful with quietness, than both hands full with labour and pursuit of the wind.
texts.ecc.4.7: And I returned and saw vanity under the sun.
texts.ecc.4.8: There is one [alone] and without a second; also he hath neither son nor brother: yet is there no end of all his labour, neither is his eye satisfied with riches, and [he saith not], For whom then am I labouring, and depriving my soul of good? This also is vanity and a grievous occupation.
texts.ecc.4.9: Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour.
texts.ecc.4.10: For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow; but woe to him that is alone when he falleth, and who hath not another to lift him up!
texts.ecc.4.11: Again, if two lie together, then they have warmth; but how can one alone be warm?
texts.ecc.4.12: And if a [man] overpower the one, the two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
texts.ecc.4.13: Better is a poor but wise youth than an old and foolish king, who knoweth no more how to be admonished.
texts.ecc.4.14: For out of the prison-house he came forth to reign, although he was born poor in his kingdom.
texts.ecc.4.15: I saw all the living that walk under the sun, with the child, the second, that should stand up in his stead.
texts.ecc.4.16: [There is] no end of all the people, of all that stood before them; those however that come after shall not rejoice in him. Surely this also is vanity and a striving after the wind.
texts.ecc.5.1: Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God, and draw near to hear, rather than to give the sacrifice of fools: for they know not that they do evil.
texts.ecc.5.2: Be not rash with thy mouth, and let not thy heart be hasty to utter anything before God: for God is in the heavens, and thou upon earth; therefore let thy words be few.
texts.ecc.5.3: For a dream cometh through the multitude of business, and a fool's voice through a multitude of words.
texts.ecc.5.4: When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed.
texts.ecc.5.5: Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.
texts.ecc.5.6: Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin; neither say thou before the angel, that it was an inadvertence. Wherefore should God be wroth at thy voice, and destroy the work of thy hands?
texts.ecc.5.7: For in the multitude of dreams are vanities; so with many words: but fear God.
texts.ecc.5.8: If thou seest the oppression of the poor, and violent perverting of judgment and justice in a province, marvel not at the matter; for a higher than the high is watching, and there are higher than they.
texts.ecc.5.9: Moreover the earth is every way profitable: the king [himself] is dependent upon the field.
texts.ecc.5.10: He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver, nor he that loveth abundance with increase. This also is vanity.
texts.ecc.5.11: When goods increase, they are increased that eat them; and what profit is there to the owner thereof, except the beholding [of them] with his eyes?
texts.ecc.5.12: The sleep of the labourer is sweet, whether he have eaten little or much; but the fulness of the rich doth not suffer him to sleep.
texts.ecc.5.13: There is a grievous evil that I have seen under the sun: riches kept for the owners thereof to their hurt;
texts.ecc.5.14: or those riches perish by some evil circumstance, and if he have begotten a son, there is nothing in his hand.
texts.ecc.5.15: As he came forth from his mother's womb, naked shall he go away again as he came, and shall take nothing of his labour, which he may carry away in his hand.
texts.ecc.5.16: And this also is a grievous evil, that in all points as he came so doth he go away, and what profit hath he, in having laboured for the wind?
texts.ecc.5.17: All his days also he eateth in darkness, and hath much vexation, and sickness, and irritation.
texts.ecc.5.18: Behold what I have seen good and comely: [it is] to eat and to drink, and to enjoy good in all his labour wherewith [man] laboureth under the sun, all the days of his life which God hath given him: for that is his portion.
texts.ecc.5.19: Every man also to whom God hath given riches and wealth, and power to eat thereof, and to take his portion and to rejoice in his labour: that is a gift of God.
texts.ecc.5.20: For he will not much remember the days of his life, because God answereth [him] with the joy of his heart.
texts.ecc.6.1: There is an evil that I have seen under the sun, and it is frequent among men:
texts.ecc.6.2: one to whom God giveth riches, wealth, and honour, and he wanteth nothing for his soul of all that he desireth, yet God giveth him not power to eat thereof, but a stranger eateth it: this is vanity, and a sore evil.
texts.ecc.6.3: If a man beget a hundred [sons], and live many years, so that the days of his years be many, but his soul be not filled with good, and also he have no burial, I say an untimely birth is better than he.
texts.ecc.6.4: For it cometh in vanity, and departeth in darkness, and its name is covered with darkness;
texts.ecc.6.5: moreover it hath not seen nor known the sun: this hath rest rather than the other.
texts.ecc.6.6: Yea, though he live twice a thousand years, yet hath he seen no good: do not all go to one place?
texts.ecc.6.7: All the labour of man is for his mouth, and yet the appetite is not filled.
texts.ecc.6.8: For what advantage hath the wise above the fool? what hath the poor, that knoweth to walk before the living?
texts.ecc.6.9: Better is the seeing of the eyes than the wandering of the desire: this also is vanity and pursuit of the wind.
texts.ecc.6.10: That which is hath already been named; and what man is, is known, and that he cannot contend with him that is mightier than he.
texts.ecc.6.11: For there are many things that increase vanity: what is man advantaged?
texts.ecc.6.12: For who knoweth what is good for man in life, all the days of his vain life which he spendeth as a shadow? for who can tell man what shall be after him under the sun?
texts.ecc.7.1: A [good] name is better than precious ointment, and the day of death than the day of one's birth.
texts.ecc.7.2: It is better to go to the house of mourning than to go to the house of feasting: in that that is the end of all men, and the living taketh it to heart.
texts.ecc.7.3: Vexation is better than laughter; for by the sadness of the countenance the heart is made better.
texts.ecc.7.4: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning, but the heart of fools in the house of mirth.
texts.ecc.7.5: It is better for a man to hear the rebuke of the wise, than to hear the song of fools.
texts.ecc.7.6: For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of the fool. This also is vanity.
texts.ecc.7.7: Surely oppression maketh a wise man mad, and a gift destroyeth the heart.
texts.ecc.7.8: Better is the end of a thing than its beginning; better is a patient spirit than a proud spirit.
texts.ecc.7.9: Be not hasty in thy spirit to be vexed; for vexation resteth in the bosom of fools.
texts.ecc.7.10: Say not, How is it that the former days were better than these? for thou dost not inquire wisely concerning this.
texts.ecc.7.11: Wisdom is as good as an inheritance, and profitable to them that see the sun.
texts.ecc.7.12: For wisdom is a defence [as] money is a defence; but the excellency of knowledge is, [that] wisdom maketh them that possess it to live.
texts.ecc.7.13: Consider the work of God; for who can make straight what he hath made crooked?
texts.ecc.7.14: In the day of prosperity enjoy good, and in the day of adversity consider: God hath also set the one beside the other, to the end that man should find out nothing [of what shall be] after him.
texts.ecc.7.15: All [this] have I seen in the days of my vanity: there is a righteous [man] that perisheth by his righteousness, and there is a wicked [man] that prolongeth [his days] by his wickedness.
texts.ecc.7.16: Be not righteous overmuch; neither make thyself overwise: why shouldest thou destroy thyself?
texts.ecc.7.17: Be not overmuch wicked, neither be thou foolish: why shouldest thou die before thy time?
texts.ecc.7.18: It is good that thou shouldest take hold of this; yea, also from that withdraw not thy hand: for he that feareth God cometh forth from them all.
texts.ecc.7.19: Wisdom strengtheneth the wise more than ten mighty [men] that are in a city.
texts.ecc.7.20: Surely there is not a righteous man upon earth, that doeth good and sinneth not.
texts.ecc.7.21: Also give not heed unto all words that are spoken, lest thou hear thy servant curse thee.
texts.ecc.7.22: For also thine own heart knoweth that oftentimes thou thyself likewise hast cursed others.
texts.ecc.7.23: All this have I tried by wisdom: I said, I will be wise; but it was far from me.
texts.ecc.7.24: Whatever hath been, is far off, and exceeding deep: who will find it out?
texts.ecc.7.25: I turned, I and my heart, to know, and to search, and to seek out wisdom and reason, and to know wickedness to be folly, and foolishness to be madness;
texts.ecc.7.26: and I found more bitter than death the woman whose heart is nets and snares, [and] whose hands are bands: whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her; but the sinner shall be caught by her.
texts.ecc.7.27: See this which I have found, saith the Preacher, [searching] one by one to find out the reason;
texts.ecc.7.28: which my soul yet seeketh, and I have not found: one man among a thousand have I found, but a woman among all those have I not found.
texts.ecc.7.29: Only see this which I have found: that God made man upright, but they have sought out many devices.
texts.ecc.8.1: Who is as the wise? and who knoweth the explanation of things? A man's wisdom maketh his face to shine, and the boldness of his face is changed.
texts.ecc.8.2: I [say], Keep the king's commandment, and [that] on account of the oath of God.
texts.ecc.8.3: Be not hasty to go out of his sight; persist not in an evil thing: for he doeth whatever pleaseth him,
texts.ecc.8.4: because the word of a king is power; and who may say unto him, What doest thou?
texts.ecc.8.5: Whoso keepeth the commandment shall know no evil thing; and a wise man's heart knoweth time and manner.
texts.ecc.8.6: For to every purpose there is time and manner. For the misery of man is great upon him;
texts.ecc.8.7: for he knoweth not that which shall be; for who can tell him how it shall be?
texts.ecc.8.8: There is no man who hath control over the spirit to retain the spirit; and no one hath control over the day of death; and there is no discharge in that war, neither shall wickedness deliver those that are given to it.
texts.ecc.8.9: All this have I seen, and applied my heart unto every work that is done under the sun: there is a time when man ruleth man to his hurt.
texts.ecc.8.10: And I have also seen the wicked buried and going away; and such as had acted rightly went from [the] holy place, and were forgotten in the city. This also is vanity.
texts.ecc.8.11: Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the children of men is fully set in them to do evil.
texts.ecc.8.12: Though a sinner do evil a hundred times, and prolong his [days], yet I know that it shall be well with them that fear God, because they fear before him;
texts.ecc.8.13: but it shall not be well with the wicked, neither shall he prolong [his] days as a shadow, because he feareth not before God.
texts.ecc.8.14: There is a vanity which is done upon the earth; that there are righteous [men] unto whom it happeneth according to the work of the wicked; and there are wicked [men] to whom it happeneth according to the work of the righteous. I said that this also is vanity.
texts.ecc.8.15: And I commended mirth, because there is nothing better for man under the sun than to eat, and to drink, and to be merry; for that shall abide with him of his labour the days of his life, which God hath given him under the sun.
texts.ecc.8.16: When I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to see the business that is done upon the earth (for also there is that neither day nor night seeth sleep with his eyes),
