texts.ecc.8.17: then I saw that all [is] the work of God, [and] that man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun: because however man may labour to seek [it] out, yet doth he not find [it]; and even, if a wise [man] think to know [it], he shall not be able to find [it] out.
texts.ecc.9.1: For all this I laid to my heart and [indeed] to investigate all this, that the righteous, and the wise, and their works, are in the hand of God; man knoweth neither love nor hatred: all is before them.
texts.ecc.9.2: All things [come] alike to all: one event to the righteous and to the wicked, to the good, and to the clean, and to the unclean, to him that sacrificeth and to him that sacrificeth not: as is the good, so is the sinner; he that sweareth, as he that feareth an oath.
texts.ecc.9.3: This is an evil among all that is done under the sun, that one thing befalleth all: yea, also the heart of the children of men is full of evil, and madness is in their heart while they live; and after that, [they have to go] to the dead.
texts.ecc.9.4: For to him that is joined to all the living there is hope; for a living dog is better than a dead lion.
texts.ecc.9.5: For the living know that they shall die; but the dead know not anything, neither have they any more a reward, for the memory of them is forgotten.
texts.ecc.9.6: Their love also, and their hatred, and their envy is already perished; neither have they any more for ever a portion in all that is done under the sun.
texts.ecc.9.7: Go, eat thy bread with joy, and drink thy wine with a merry heart; for God hath already accepted thy works.
texts.ecc.9.8: Let thy garments be always white, and let not thy head lack oil.
texts.ecc.9.9: Enjoy life with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, which he hath given thee under the sun, all the days of thy vanity; for that is thy portion in life, and in thy labour wherein thou art labouring under the sun.
texts.ecc.9.10: Whatever thy hand findeth to do, do with thy might; for there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in Sheol, whither thou goest.
texts.ecc.9.11: I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to the intelligent, nor yet favour to men of knowledge; but time and chance happeneth to them all.
texts.ecc.9.12: For man also knoweth not his time: as the fishes that are taken in an evil net, and as the birds that are taken with the snare, like them are the children of men snared in an evil time, when it falleth suddenly upon them.
texts.ecc.9.13: This also have I seen as wisdom under the sun, and it was great unto me.
texts.ecc.9.14: There was a little city, and few men within it; and there came a great king against it, and encompassed it, and built great bulwarks against it:
texts.ecc.9.15: and there was found in it a poor wise man, who by his wisdom delivered the city; but no man remembered that poor man.
texts.ecc.9.16: Then said I, Wisdom is better than strength; but the poor man's wisdom is despised, and his words are not heard.
texts.ecc.9.17: The words of the wise are heard in quiet more than the cry of him that ruleth among fools.
texts.ecc.9.18: Wisdom is better than weapons of war; but one sinner destroyeth much good.
texts.ecc.10.1: Dead flies cause the ointment of the apothecary to stink [and] ferment; [so] a little folly is weightier than wisdom [and] honour.
texts.ecc.10.2: The heart of a wise [man] is at his right hand; but a fool's heart at his left.
texts.ecc.10.3: Yea also, when he that is a fool walketh by the way, his sense faileth [him], and he saith to every one [that] he is a fool.
texts.ecc.10.4: If the spirit of the ruler rise up against thee, leave not thy place; for quietness pacifieth great offences.
texts.ecc.10.5: There is an evil that I have seen under the sun, as an error [that] proceedeth from the ruler:
texts.ecc.10.6: folly is set in great dignities, but the rich sit in a low place.
texts.ecc.10.7: I have seen servants upon horses, and princes walking as servants upon the earth.
texts.ecc.10.8: He that diggeth a pit falleth into it; and whoso breaketh down a hedge, a serpent biteth him.
texts.ecc.10.9: Whoso removeth stones is hurt therewith; he that cleaveth wood is endangered thereby.
texts.ecc.10.10: If the iron be blunt, and one do not whet the edge, then must he apply more strength; but wisdom is profitable to give success.
texts.ecc.10.11: If the serpent bite before enchantment, then the charmer hath no advantage.
texts.ecc.10.12: The words of a wise man's mouth are gracious; but the lips of a fool swallow up himself.
texts.ecc.10.13: The beginning of the words of his mouth is folly; and the end of his talk is mischievous madness.
texts.ecc.10.14: And the fool multiplieth words: [yet] man knoweth not what shall be; and what shall be after him, who will tell him?
texts.ecc.10.15: The labour of fools wearieth them, because they know not how to go to the city.
texts.ecc.10.16: Woe to thee, O land, when thy king is a child, and thy princes eat in the morning!
texts.ecc.10.17: Happy art thou, O land, when thy king is a son of nobles, and thy princes eat in [due] season, for strength, and not for drunkenness!
texts.ecc.10.18: By much sloth fulness the framework falleth in; and through idleness of the hands the house drippeth.
texts.ecc.10.19: A feast is made for laughter, and wine maketh life merry; but money answereth everything.
texts.ecc.10.20: Curse not the king, no, not in thy thought; and curse not the rich in thy bedchamber: for the bird of the air will carry the voice, and that which hath wings will tell the matter.
texts.ecc.11.1: Cast thy bread upon the waters; for thou shalt find it after many days.
texts.ecc.11.2: Give a portion to seven, and also to eight; for thou knowest not what evil shall be upon the earth.
texts.ecc.11.3: If the clouds be full of rain, they empty themselves upon the earth; and if a tree fall toward the south, or toward the north, in the place where the tree falleth, there it shall be.
texts.ecc.11.4: He that observeth the wind will not sow; and he that regardeth the clouds will not reap.
texts.ecc.11.5: As thou knowest not what is the way of the spirit, how the bones [grow] in the womb of her that is with child, even so thou knowest not the work of God who maketh all.
texts.ecc.11.6: In the morning sow thy seed, and in the evening withhold not thy hand; for thou knowest not which shall prosper, whether this or that, or whether they both shall be alike good.
texts.ecc.11.7: Now the light is sweet, and pleasant is it to the eyes to see the sun;
texts.ecc.11.8: but if a man live many years, [and] rejoice in them all, yet let him remember the days of darkness; for they shall be many: all that cometh is vanity.
texts.ecc.11.9: Rejoice, young man, in thy youth; and let thy heart cheer thee in the days of thy youth, and walk in the ways of thy heart, and in the sight of thine eyes; but know that for all these [things] God will bring thee into judgment.
texts.ecc.11.10: Then remove discontent from thy heart, and put away evil from thy flesh; for childhood and youth are vanity.
texts.ecc.12.1: And remember thy Creator in the days of thy youth, before the evil days come, and the years draw nigh, of which thou shalt say, I have no pleasure in them;
texts.ecc.12.2: before the sun, and the light, and the moon, and the stars, be darkened, and the clouds return after the rain;
texts.ecc.12.3: in the day when the keepers of the house tremble, and the strong men bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those that look out of the windows are darkened,
texts.ecc.12.4: and the doors are shut toward the street; when the sound of the grinding is subdued, and they rise up at the voice of the bird, and all the daughters of song are brought low;
texts.ecc.12.5: they are also afraid of what is high, and terrors are in the way, and the almond is despised, and the grasshopper is a burden, and the caper-berry is without effect; (for man goeth to his age-long home, and the mourners go about the streets;)
texts.ecc.12.6: -- before the silver cord be loosed, or the golden bowl be broken, or the pitcher be shattered at the fountain, or the wheel be broken at the cistern;
texts.ecc.12.7: and the dust return to the earth as it was, and the spirit return unto God who gave it.
texts.ecc.12.8: Vanity of vanities, saith the Preacher: all is vanity.
texts.ecc.12.9: And moreover, because the Preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge; and he pondered, and sought out, [and] set in order many proverbs.
texts.ecc.12.10: The Preacher sought to find out acceptable words; and that which was written is upright, words of truth.
texts.ecc.12.11: The words of the wise are as goads, and the collections [of them] as nails fastened in: they are given from one shepherd.
texts.ecc.12.12: And besides, my son, be warned by them: of making many books there is no end, and much study is a weariness of the flesh.
texts.ecc.12.13: Let us hear the end of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments; for this is the whole of man.
texts.ecc.12.14: For God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good or whether it be evil.

texts.ecc.1.1: Words of a preacher, son of David, king in Jerusalem:
texts.ecc.1.2: Vanity of vanities, said the Preacher, Vanity of vanities: the whole [is] vanity.
texts.ecc.1.3: What advantage [is] to man by all his labour that he laboureth at under the sun?
texts.ecc.1.4: A generation is going, and a generation is coming, and the earth to the age is standing.
texts.ecc.1.5: Also, the sun hath risen, and the sun hath gone in, and unto its place panting it is rising there.
texts.ecc.1.6: Going unto the south, and turning round unto the north, turning round, turning round, the wind is going, and by its circuits the wind hath returned.
texts.ecc.1.7: All the streams are going unto the sea, and the sea is not full; unto a place whither the streams are going, thither they are turning back to go.
texts.ecc.1.8: All these things are wearying; a man is not able to speak, the eye is not satisfied by seeing, nor filled is the ear from hearing.
texts.ecc.1.9: What [is] that which hath been? it [is] that which is, and what [is] that which hath been done? it [is] that which is done, and there is not an entirely new thing under the sun.
texts.ecc.1.10: There is a thing of which [one] saith: `See this, it [is] new!' already it hath been in the ages that were before us!
texts.ecc.1.11: There is not a remembrance of former [generations]; and also of the latter that are, there is no remembrance of them with those that are at the last.
texts.ecc.1.12: I, a preacher, have been king over Israel in Jerusalem.
texts.ecc.1.13: And I have given my heart to seek and to search out by wisdom concerning all that hath been done under the heavens. It [is] a sad travail God hath given to the sons of man to be humbled by it.
texts.ecc.1.14: I have seen all the works that have been done under the sun, and lo, the whole [is] vanity and vexation of spirit!
texts.ecc.1.15: A crooked thing [one] is not able to make straight, and a lacking thing is not able to be numbered.
texts.ecc.1.16: I -- I spake with my heart, saying, `I, lo, I have magnified and added wisdom above every one who hath been before me at Jerusalem, and my heart hath seen abundantly wisdom and knowledge.
texts.ecc.1.17: And I give my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly: I have known that even this [is] vexation of spirit;
texts.ecc.1.18: for, in abundance of wisdom [is] abundance of sadness, and he who addeth knowledge addeth pain.'
texts.ecc.2.1: I said in my heart, `Pray, come, I try thee with mirth, and look thou on gladness;' and lo, even it [is] vanity.
texts.ecc.2.2: Of laughter I said, `Foolish!' and of mirth, `What [is] this it is doing?'
texts.ecc.2.3: I have sought in my heart to draw out with wine my appetite, (and my heart leading in wisdom), and to take hold on folly till that I see where [is] this -- the good to the sons of man of that which they do under the heavens, the number of the days of their lives.
texts.ecc.2.4: I made great my works, I builded for me houses, I planted for me vineyards.
texts.ecc.2.5: I made for me gardens and paradises, and I planted in them trees of every fruit.
texts.ecc.2.6: I made for me pools of water, to water from them a forest shooting forth trees.
texts.ecc.2.7: I got men-servants, and maid-servants, and sons of the house were to me; also, I had much substance -- herd and flock -- above all who had been before me in Jerusalem.
texts.ecc.2.8: I gathered for me also silver and gold, and the peculiar treasure of kings and of the provinces. I prepared for me men-singers and women-singers, and the luxuries of the sons of man -- a wife and wives.
texts.ecc.2.9: And I became great, and increased above every one who had been before me in Jerusalem; also, my wisdom stood with me.
texts.ecc.2.10: And all that mine eyes asked I kept not back from them; I withheld not my heart from any joy, for my heart rejoiced because of all my labour, and this hath been my portion, from all my labour,
texts.ecc.2.11: and I have looked on all my works that my hands have done, and on the labour that I have laboured to do, and lo, the whole [is] vanity and vexation of spirit, and there is no advantage under the sun!
texts.ecc.2.12: And I turned to see wisdom, and madness, and folly, but what [is] the man who cometh after the king? that which [is] already -- they have done it!
texts.ecc.2.13: And I saw that there is an advantage to wisdom above folly, like the advantage of the light above the darkness.
texts.ecc.2.14: The wise! -- his eyes [are] in his head, and the fool in darkness is walking, and I also knew that one event happeneth with them all;
texts.ecc.2.15: and I said in my heart, `As it happeneth with the fool, it happeneth also with me, and why am I then more wise?' And I spake in my heart, that also this [is] vanity:
texts.ecc.2.16: That there is no remembrance to the wise -- with the fool -- to the age, for that which [is] already, [in] the days that are coming is all forgotten, and how dieth the wise? with the fool!
texts.ecc.2.17: And I have hated life, for sad to me [is] the work that hath been done under the sun, for the whole [is] vanity and vexation of spirit.
texts.ecc.2.18: And I have hated all my labour that I labour at under the sun, because I leave it to a man who is after me.
texts.ecc.2.19: And who knoweth whether he is wise or foolish? yet he doth rule over all my labour that I have laboured at, and that I have done wisely under the sun! this also [is] vanity.
texts.ecc.2.20: And I turned round to cause my heart to despair concerning all the labour that I laboured at under the sun.
texts.ecc.2.21: For there is a man whose labour [is] in wisdom, and in knowledge, and in equity, and to a man who hath not laboured therein he giveth it -- his portion! Even this [is] vanity and a great evil.
texts.ecc.2.22: For what hath been to a man by all his labour, and by the thought of his heart that he laboured at under the sun?
texts.ecc.2.23: For all his days are sorrows, and his travail sadness; even at night his heart hath not lain down; this also [is] vanity.
texts.ecc.2.24: There is nothing good in a man who eateth, and hath drunk, and hath shewn his soul good in his labour. This also I have seen that it [is] from the hand of God.
texts.ecc.2.25: For who eateth and who hasteth out more than I?
texts.ecc.2.26: For to a man who [is] good before Him, He hath given wisdom, and knowledge, and joy; and to a sinner He hath given travail, to gather and to heap up, to give to the good before God. Even this [is] vanity and vexation of spirit.
texts.ecc.3.1: To everything -- a season, and a time to every delight under the heavens:
texts.ecc.3.2: A time to bring forth, And a time to die. A time to plant, And a time to eradicate the planted.
texts.ecc.3.3: A time to slay, And a time to heal, A time to break down, And a time to build up.
texts.ecc.3.4: A time to weep, And a time to laugh. A time to mourn, And a time to skip.
texts.ecc.3.5: A time to cast away stones, And a time to heap up stones. A time to embrace, And a time to be far from embracing.
texts.ecc.3.6: A time to seek, And a time to destroy. A time to keep, And a time to cast away.
texts.ecc.3.7: A time to rend, And a time to sew. A time to be silent, And a time to speak.
texts.ecc.3.8: A time to love, And a time to hate. A time of war, And a time of peace.
texts.ecc.3.9: What advantage hath the doer in that which he is labouring at?
texts.ecc.3.10: I have seen the travail that God hath given to the sons of man to be humbled by it.
texts.ecc.3.11: The whole He hath made beautiful in its season; also, that knowledge He hath put in their heart without which man findeth not out the work that God hath done from the beginning even unto the end.
texts.ecc.3.12: I have known that there is no good for them except to rejoice and to do good during their life,
texts.ecc.3.13: yea, even every man who eateth and hath drunk and seen good by all his labour, it [is] a gift of God.
texts.ecc.3.14: I have known that all that God doth is to the age, to it nothing is to be added, and from it nothing is to be withdrawn; and God hath wrought that they do fear before Him.
texts.ecc.3.15: What is that which hath been? already it is, and that which [is] to be hath already been, and God requireth that which is pursued.
texts.ecc.3.16: And again, I have seen under the sun the place of judgment -- there [is] the wicked; and the place of righteousness -- there [is] the wicked.
texts.ecc.3.17: I said in my heart, `The righteous and the wicked doth God judge, for a time [is] to every matter and for every work there.'
texts.ecc.3.18: I said in my heart concerning the matter of the sons of man that God might cleanse them, so as to see that they themselves [are] beasts.
texts.ecc.3.19: For an event [is to] the sons of man, and an event [is to] the beasts, even one event [is] to them; as the death of this, so [is] the death of that; and one spirit [is] to all, and the advantage of man above the beast is nothing, for the whole [is] vanity.
texts.ecc.3.20: The whole are going unto one place, the whole have been from the dust, and the whole are turning back unto the dust.
texts.ecc.3.21: Who knoweth the spirit of the sons of man that is going up on high, and the spirit of the beast that is going down below to the earth?
texts.ecc.3.22: And I have seen that there is nothing better than that man rejoice in his works, for it [is] his portion; for who doth bring him in to look on that which is after him?
texts.ecc.4.1: And I have turned, and I see all the oppressions that are done under the sun, and lo, the tear of the oppressed, and they have no comforter; and at the hand of their oppressors [is] power, and they have no comforter.
texts.ecc.4.2: And I am praising the dead who have already died above the living who are yet alive.
texts.ecc.4.3: And better than both of them [is] he who hath not yet been, in that he hath not seen the evil work that hath been done under the sun.
texts.ecc.4.4: And I have seen all the labour, and all the benefit of the work, because for it a man is the envy of his neighbour. Even this [is] vanity and vexation of spirit.
texts.ecc.4.5: The fool is clasping his hands, and eating his own flesh:
texts.ecc.4.6: `Better [is] a handful [with] quietness, than two handfuls [with] labour and vexation of spirit.'
texts.ecc.4.7: And I have turned, and I see a vain thing under the sun:
texts.ecc.4.8: There is one, and there is not a second; even son or brother he hath not, and there is no end to all his labour! His eye also is not satisfied with riches, and [he saith not], `For whom am I labouring and bereaving my soul of good?' This also is vanity, it is a sad travail.
texts.ecc.4.9: The two [are] better than the one, in that they have a good reward by their labour.
texts.ecc.4.10: For if they fall, the one raiseth up his companion, but wo to the one who falleth and there is not a second to raise him up!
texts.ecc.4.11: Also, if two lie down, then they have heat, but how hath one heat?
texts.ecc.4.12: And if the one strengthen himself, the two stand against him; and the threefold cord is not hastily broken.
texts.ecc.4.13: Better is a poor and wise youth than an old and foolish king, who hath not known to be warned any more.
texts.ecc.4.14: For from a house of prisoners he hath come out to reign, for even in his own kingdom he hath been poor.
texts.ecc.4.15: I have seen all the living, who are walking under the sun, with the second youth who doth stand in his place;
texts.ecc.4.16: there is no end to all the people, to all who were before them; also, the latter rejoice not in him. Surely this also is vanity and vexation of spirit.
texts.ecc.5.1: Keep thy feet when thou goest unto a house of God, and draw near to hear rather than to give of fools the sacrifice, for they do not know they do evil.
texts.ecc.5.2: Cause not thy mouth to hasten, and let not thy heart hasten to bring out a word before God, for God is in the heavens, and thou on the earth, therefore let thy words be few.
texts.ecc.5.3: For the dream hath come by abundance of business, and the voice of a fool by abundance of words.
texts.ecc.5.4: When thou vowest a vow to God, delay not to complete it, for there is no pleasure in fools; that which thou vowest -- complete.
texts.ecc.5.5: Better that thou do not vow, than that thou dost vow and dost not complete.
texts.ecc.5.6: Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin, nor say before the messenger, that `it [is] an error,' why is God wroth because of thy voice, and hath destroyed the work of thy hands?
texts.ecc.5.7: For, in the abundance of dreams both vanities and words abound; but fear thou God.
texts.ecc.5.8: If oppression of the poor, and violent taking away of judgment and righteousness thou seest in a province, do not marvel at the matter, for a higher than the high is observing, and high ones [are] over them.
texts.ecc.5.9: And the abundance of a land is for all. A king for a field is served.
texts.ecc.5.10: Whoso is loving silver is not satisfied [with] silver, nor he who is in love with stores [with] increase. Even this [is] vanity.
texts.ecc.5.11: In the multiplying of good have its consumers been multiplied, and what benefit [is] to its possessor except the sight of his eyes?
texts.ecc.5.12: Sweet [is] the sleep of the labourer whether he eat little or much; and the sufficiency of the wealthy is not suffering him to sleep.
texts.ecc.5.13: There is a painful evil I have seen under the sun: wealth kept for its possessor, for his evil.
texts.ecc.5.14: And that wealth hath been lost in an evil business, and he hath begotten a son and there is nothing in his hand!
texts.ecc.5.15: As he came out from the belly of his mother, naked he turneth back to go as he came, and he taketh not away anything of his labour, that doth go in his hand.
texts.ecc.5.16: And this also [is] a painful evil, just as he came, so he goeth, and what advantage [is] to him who laboureth for wind?
texts.ecc.5.17: Also all his days in darkness he consumeth, and sadness, and wrath, and sickness abound.
texts.ecc.5.18: Lo, that which I have seen: [It is] good, because beautiful, to eat, and to drink, and to see good in all one's labour that he laboureth at under the sun, the number of the days of his life that God hath given to him, for it [is] his portion.
texts.ecc.5.19: Every man also to whom God hath given wealth and riches, and hath given him power to eat of it, and to accept his portion, and to rejoice in his labour, this is a gift of God.
texts.ecc.5.20: For he doth not much remember the days of his life, for God is answering through the joy of his heart.
texts.ecc.6.1: There is an evil that I have seen under the sun, and it [is] great on man:
texts.ecc.6.2: A man to whom God giveth wealth, and riches, and honour, and there is no lack to his soul of all that he desireth, and God giveth him not power to eat of it, but a stranger eateth it; this [is] vanity, and it [is] an evil disease.
texts.ecc.6.3: If a man doth beget a hundred, and live many years, and is great, because they are the days of his years, and his soul is not satisfied from the goodness, and also he hath not had a grave, I have said, `Better than he [is] the untimely birth.'
texts.ecc.6.4: For in vanity he came in, and in darkness he goeth, and in darkness his name is covered,
texts.ecc.6.5: Even the sun he hath not seen nor known, more rest hath this than that.
texts.ecc.6.6: And though he had lived a thousand years twice over, yet good he hath not seen; to the same place doth not every one go?
texts.ecc.6.7: All the labour of man [is] for his mouth, and yet the soul is not filled.
texts.ecc.6.8: For what advantage [is] to the wise above the fool? What to the poor who knoweth to walk before the living?
texts.ecc.6.9: Better [is] the sight of the eyes than the going of the soul. This also [is] vanity and vexation of spirit.
texts.ecc.6.10: What [is] that which hath been? already is its name called, and it is known that it [is] man, and he is not able to contend with him who is stronger than he.
texts.ecc.6.11: For there are many things multiplying vanity; what advantage [is] to man?
texts.ecc.6.12: For who knoweth what [is] good for a man in life, the number of the days of the life of his vanity, and he maketh them as a shadow? for who declareth to man what is after him under the sun?
texts.ecc.7.1: Better [is] a name than good perfume, And the day of death than the day of birth.
texts.ecc.7.2: Better to go unto a house of mourning, Than to go unto a house of banqueting, For that is the end of all men, And the living layeth [it] unto his heart.
texts.ecc.7.3: Better [is] sorrow than laughter, For by the sadness of the face the heart becometh better.
texts.ecc.7.4: The heart of the wise [is] in a house of mourning, And the heart of fools in a house of mirth.
texts.ecc.7.5: Better to hear a rebuke of a wise man, Than [for] a man to hear a song of fools,
texts.ecc.7.6: For as the noise of thorns under the pot, So [is] the laughter of a fool, even this [is] vanity.
texts.ecc.7.7: Surely oppression maketh the wise mad, And a gift destroyeth the heart.
texts.ecc.7.8: Better [is] the latter end of a thing than its beginning, Better [is] the patient of spirit, than the haughty of spirit.
texts.ecc.7.9: Be not hasty in thy spirit to be angry, For anger in the bosom of fools resteth.
texts.ecc.7.10: Say not thou, `What was it, That the former days were better than these?' For thou hast not asked wisely of this.
texts.ecc.7.11: Wisdom [is] good with an inheritance, And an advantage [it is] to those beholding the sun.
texts.ecc.7.12: For wisdom [is] a defense, money [is] a defence, And the advantage of the knowledge of wisdom [is], She reviveth her possessors.
texts.ecc.7.13: See the work of God, For who is able to make straight that which He made crooked?
texts.ecc.7.14: In a day of prosperity be in gladness, And in a day of evil consider. Also this over-against that hath God made, To the intent that man doth not find anything after him.
texts.ecc.7.15: The whole I have considered in the days of my vanity. There is a righteous one perishing in his righteousness, and there is a wrong-doer prolonging [himself] in his wrong.
texts.ecc.7.16: Be not over-righteous, nor show thyself too wise, why art thou desolate?
texts.ecc.7.17: Do not much wrong, neither be thou a fool, why dost thou die within thy time?
texts.ecc.7.18: [It is] good that thou dost lay hold on this, and also, from that withdrawest not thy hand, for whoso is fearing God goeth out with them all.
texts.ecc.7.19: The wisdom giveth strength to a wise man, more than wealth the rulers who have been in a city.
texts.ecc.7.20: Because there is not a righteous man on earth that doth good and sinneth not.
texts.ecc.7.21: Also to all the words that they speak give not thy heart, that thou hear not thy servant reviling thee.
texts.ecc.7.22: For many times also hath thy heart known that thou thyself also hast reviled others.
texts.ecc.7.23: All this I have tried by wisdom; I have said, `I am wise,' and it [is] far from me.
texts.ecc.7.24: Far off [is] that which hath been, and deep, deep, who doth find it?
texts.ecc.7.25: I have turned round, also my heart, to know and to search, and to seek out wisdom, and reason, and to know the wrong of folly, and of foolishness the madness.
texts.ecc.7.26: And I am finding more bitter than death, the woman whose heart [is] nets and snares, her hands [are] bands; the good before God escapeth from her, but the sinner is captured by her.
texts.ecc.7.27: See, this I have found, said the Preacher, one to one, to find out the reason
texts.ecc.7.28: (that still my soul had sought, and I had not found), One man, a teacher, I have found, and a woman among all these I have not found.
texts.ecc.7.29: See, this alone I have found, that God made man upright, and they -- they have sought out many devices.
texts.ecc.8.1: Who [is] as the wise? and who knoweth the interpretation of a thing? The wisdom of man causeth his face to shine, and the hardness of his face is changed.
texts.ecc.8.2: I pray thee, the commandment of a king keep, even for the sake of the oath of God.
texts.ecc.8.3: Be not troubled at his presence, thou mayest go, stand not in an evil thing, for all that he pleaseth he doth.
texts.ecc.8.4: Where the word of a king [is] power [is], and who saith to him, `What dost thou?'
texts.ecc.8.5: Whoso is keeping a command knoweth no evil thing, and time and judgment the heart of the wise knoweth.
texts.ecc.8.6: For to every delight there is a time and a judgment, for the misfortune of man is great upon him.
texts.ecc.8.7: For he knoweth not that which shall be, for when it shall be who declareth to him?
texts.ecc.8.8: There is no man ruling over the spirit to restrain the spirit, and there is no authority over the day of death, and there is no discharge in battle, and wickedness delivereth not its possessors.
texts.ecc.8.9: All this I have seen so as to give my heart to every work that hath been done under the sun; a time that man hath ruled over man to his own evil.
texts.ecc.8.10: And so I have seen the wicked buried, and they went in, even from the Holy Place they go, and they are forgotten in the city whether they had so done. This also [is] vanity.
texts.ecc.8.11: Because sentence hath not been done [on] an evil work speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of man is full within them to do evil.
texts.ecc.8.12: Though a sinner is doing evil a hundred [times], and prolonging [himself] for it, surely also I know that there is good to those fearing God, who fear before Him.
texts.ecc.8.13: And good is not to the wicked, and he doth not prolong days as a shadow, because he is not fearing before God.
texts.ecc.8.14: There is a vanity that hath been done upon the earth, that there are righteous ones unto whom it is coming according to the work of the wicked, and there are wicked ones unto whom it is coming according to the work of the righteous. I have said that this also [is] vanity.
texts.ecc.8.15: And I have praised mirth because there is no good to man under the sun except to eat and to drink, and to rejoice, and it remaineth with him of his labour the days of his life that God hath given to him under the sun.
texts.ecc.8.16: When I gave my heart to know wisdom and to see the business that hath been done on the earth, (for there is also a spectator in whose eyes sleep is not by day and by night),
texts.ecc.8.17: then I considered all the work of God, that man is not able to find out the work that hath been done under the sun, because though man labour to seek, yet he doth not find; and even though the wise man speak of knowing he is not able to find.
texts.ecc.9.1: But all this I have laid unto my heart, so as to clear up the whole of this, that the righteous and the wise, and their works, [are] in the hand of God, neither love nor hatred doth man know, the whole [is] before them.
texts.ecc.9.2: The whole [is] as to the whole; one event is to the righteous and to the wicked, to the good, and to the clean, and to the unclean, and to him who is sacrificing, and to him who is not sacrificing; as [is] the good, so [is] the sinner, he who is swearing as he who is fearing an oath.
texts.ecc.9.3: This [is] an evil among all that hath been done under the sun, that one event [is] to all, and also the heart of the sons of man is full of evil, and madness [is] in their heart during their life, and after it -- unto the dead.
texts.ecc.9.4: But [to] him who is joined unto all the living there is confidence, for to a living dog it [is] better than to the dead lion.
texts.ecc.9.5: For the living know that they die, and the dead know not anything, and there is no more to them a reward, for their remembrance hath been forgotten.
texts.ecc.9.6: Their love also, their hatred also, their envy also, hath already perished, and they have no more a portion to the age in all that hath been done under the sun.
texts.ecc.9.7: Go, eat with joy thy bread, and drink with a glad heart thy wine, for already hath God been pleased with thy works.
texts.ecc.9.8: At all times let thy garments be white, and let not perfume be lacking on thy head.
texts.ecc.9.9: See life with the wife whom thou hast loved, all the days of the life of thy vanity, that He hath given to thee under the sun, all the days of thy vanity, for it [is] thy portion in life, even of thy labour that thou art labouring at under the sun.
texts.ecc.9.10: All that thy hand findeth to do, with thy power do, for there is no work, and device, and knowledge, and wisdom in Sheol whither thou art going.
texts.ecc.9.11: I have turned so as to see under the sun, that not to the swift [is] the race, nor to the mighty the battle, nor even to the wise bread, nor even to the intelligent wealth, nor even to the skilful grace, for time and chance happen with them all.
texts.ecc.9.12: For even man knoweth not his time; as fish that are taken hold of by an evil net, and as birds that are taken hold of by a snare, like these [are] the sons of man snared at an evil time, when it falleth upon them suddenly.
texts.ecc.9.13: This also I have seen: wisdom under the sun, and it is great to me.
texts.ecc.9.14: A little city, and few men in it, and a great king hath come unto it, and hath surrounded it, and hath built against it great bulwarks;
texts.ecc.9.15: and there hath been found in it a poor wise man, and he hath delivered the city by his wisdom, and men have not remembered that poor man!
texts.ecc.9.16: And I said, `Better [is] wisdom than might, and the wisdom of the poor is despised, and his words are not heard.' --
texts.ecc.9.17: The words of the wise in quiet are heard, More than the cry of a ruler over fools.
texts.ecc.9.18: Better [is] wisdom than weapons of conflict, And one sinner destroyeth much good!
texts.ecc.10.1: Dead flies cause a perfumer's perfume To send forth a stink; The precious by reason of wisdom -- By reason of honour -- a little folly!
texts.ecc.10.2: The heart of the wise [is] at his right hand, And the heart of a fool at his left.
texts.ecc.10.3: And also, when he that is a fool Is walking in the way, his heart is lacking, And he hath said to every one, `He [is] a fool.'
texts.ecc.10.4: If the spirit of the ruler go up against thee, Thy place leave not, For yielding quieteth great sinners.
texts.ecc.10.5: There is an evil I have seen under the sun, As an error that goeth out from the ruler,
texts.ecc.10.6: He hath set the fool in many high places, And the rich in a low place do sit.
texts.ecc.10.7: I have seen servants on horses, And princes walking as servants on the earth.
texts.ecc.10.8: Whoso is digging a pit falleth into it, And whoso is breaking a hedge, a serpent biteth him.
texts.ecc.10.9: Whoso is removing stones is grieved by them, Whoso is cleaving trees endangered by them.
texts.ecc.10.10: If the iron hath been blunt, And he the face hath not sharpened, Then doth he increase strength, And wisdom [is] advantageous to make right.
texts.ecc.10.11: If the serpent biteth without enchantment, Then there is no advantage to a master of the tongue.
texts.ecc.10.12: Words of the mouth of the wise [are] gracious, And the lips of a fool swallow him up.
texts.ecc.10.13: The beginning of the words of his mouth [is] folly, And the latter end of his mouth [Is] mischievous madness.
texts.ecc.10.14: And the fool multiplieth words: `Man knoweth not that which is, And that which is after him, who doth declare to him?'
texts.ecc.10.15: The labour of the foolish wearieth him, In that he hath not known to go unto the city.
texts.ecc.10.16: Wo to thee, O land, when thy king [is] a youth, And thy princes do eat in the morning.
texts.ecc.10.17: Happy art thou, O land, When thy king [is] a son of freemen, And thy princes do eat in due season, For might, and not for drunkenness.
texts.ecc.10.18: By slothfulness is the wall brought low, And by idleness of the hands doth the house drop.
texts.ecc.10.19: For mirth they are making a feast, And wine maketh life joyful, And the silver answereth with all.
texts.ecc.10.20: Even in thy mind a king revile not, And in the inner parts of thy bed-chamber Revile not the rich: For a fowl of the heavens causeth the voice to go, And a possessor of wings declareth the word.
texts.ecc.11.1: Send forth thy bread on the face of the waters, For in the multitude of the days thou dost find it.
texts.ecc.11.2: Give a portion to seven, and even to eight, For thou knowest not what evil is on the earth.
texts.ecc.11.3: If the thick clouds are full of rain, On the earth they empty [themselves]; And if a tree doth fall in the south or to the north, The place where the tree falleth, there it is.
texts.ecc.11.4: Whoso is observing the wind soweth not, And whoso is looking on the thick clouds reapeth not.
texts.ecc.11.5: As thou knowest not what [is] the way of the spirit, How -- bones in the womb of the full one, So thou knowest not the work of God who maketh the whole.
texts.ecc.11.6: In the morning sow thy seed, And at even withdraw not thy hand, For thou knowest not which is right, this or that, Or whether both of them alike [are] good.
texts.ecc.11.7: Sweet also [is] the light, And good for the eyes to see the sun.
texts.ecc.11.8: But, if man liveth many years, In all of them let him rejoice, And remember the days of darkness, For they are many! all that is coming [is] vanity.
texts.ecc.11.9: Rejoice, O young man, in thy childhood, And let thy heart gladden thee in days of thy youth, And walk in the ways of thy heart, And in the sight of thine eyes, And know thou that for all these, Doth God bring thee into judgment.
texts.ecc.11.10: And turn aside anger from thy heart, And cause evil to pass from thy flesh, For the childhood and the age [are] vanity!
texts.ecc.12.1: Remember also thy Creators in days of thy youth, While that the evil days come not, Nor the years have arrived, that thou sayest, `I have no pleasure in them.'
texts.ecc.12.2: While that the sun is not darkened, and the light, And the moon, and the stars, And the thick clouds returned after the rain.
texts.ecc.12.3: In the day that keepers of the house tremble, And men of strength have bowed themselves, And grinders have ceased, because they have become few. And those looking out at the windows have become dim,
texts.ecc.12.4: And doors have been shut in the street. When the noise of the grinding is low, And [one] riseth at the voice of the bird, And all daughters of song are bowed down.
texts.ecc.12.5: Also of that which is high they are afraid, And of the low places in the way, And the almond-tree is despised, And the grasshopper is become a burden, And want is increased, For man is going unto his home age-during, And the mourners have gone round through the street.
texts.ecc.12.6: While that the silver cord is not removed, And the golden bowl broken, And the pitcher broken by the fountain, And the wheel broken at the well.
texts.ecc.12.7: And the dust returneth to the earth as it was, And the spirit returneth to God who gave it.
texts.ecc.12.8: Vanity of vanities, said the preacher, the whole [is] vanity.
texts.ecc.12.9: And further, because the preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge, and gave ear, and sought out -- he made right many similes.
texts.ecc.12.10: The preacher sought to find out pleasing words, and, written [by] the upright, words of truth.
texts.ecc.12.11: Words of the wise [are] as goads, and as fences planted [by] the masters of collections, they have been given by one shepherd.
texts.ecc.12.12: And further, from these, my son, be warned; the making of many books hath no end, and much study [is] a weariness of the flesh.
texts.ecc.12.13: The end of the whole matter let us hear: -- `Fear God, and keep His commands, for this [is] the whole of man.
texts.ecc.12.14: For every work doth God bring into judgment, with every hidden thing, whether good or bad.'

texts.ecc.1.1: Palabras del Predicador, hijo de David, rey en Jerusalem.
texts.ecc.1.2: Vanidad de vanidades, dijo el Predicador, vanidad de vanidades; todo vanidad.
texts.ecc.1.3: ¿Qué tiene más el hombre de todo su trabajo, con que trabaja debajo del sol?
texts.ecc.1.4: Generación va, y generación viene; y la tierra siempre permanece.
texts.ecc.1.5: Y sale el sol, y pónese el sol; y como con deseo vuelve a su lugar, donde torna a nacer.
texts.ecc.1.6: El viento va al mediodía, y rodea al norte: va rodeando rodeando, y por sus rodeos torna el viento.
texts.ecc.1.7: Los ríos todos van a la mar, y la mar no se hinche: al lugar de donde los ríos vinieron, allí tornan para volver.
texts.ecc.1.8: Todas las cosas andan en trabajo, más que el hombre pueda decir; ni los ojos viendo hartarse de ver, ni los oídos oyendo henchirse.
texts.ecc.1.9: ¿Qué es lo que fue? Lo mismo que será. ¿Qué es lo que ha sido hecho? Lo mismo que se hará; y nada hay nuevo debajo del sol.
texts.ecc.1.10: Hay algo de que se pueda decir: ¿Veis aquí, esto es nuevo? Ya fue en los siglos que nos han precedido.
texts.ecc.1.11: No hay memoria de lo que precedió, ni tampoco de lo que sucederá habrá memoria en los que serán después.
texts.ecc.1.12: Yo, el Predicador, fui rey sobre Israel en Jerusalem,
texts.ecc.1.13: Y di mi corazón a inquirir y buscar con sabiduría sobre todo lo que se hace debajo del cielo: (esta mala ocupación dio Dios a los hijos de los hombres, en que se ocupen:)
texts.ecc.1.14: Yo miré todas las obras que se hacen debajo del sol; y, he aquí, que todo ello es vanidad, y aflicción de espíritu.
texts.ecc.1.15: Lo torcido no se puede enderezar; y lo falto no se puede contar.
texts.ecc.1.16: Hablé yo con mi corazón, diciendo: He aquí, yo soy engrandecido, y he crecido en sabiduría sobre todos los que fueron antes de mí en Jerusalem; y mi corazón ha visto multitud de sabiduría y de ciencia.
texts.ecc.1.17: Y di mi corazón a conocer la sabiduría, y la ciencia; y las locuras y desvaríos: conocí al cabo que aun esto era aflicción de espíritu.
texts.ecc.1.18: Porque en la mucha sabiduría hay mucho enojo; y quien añade ciencia, añade dolor.
texts.ecc.2.1: Dije yo también en mi corazón: Ahora ven acá, yo tentaré en alegría. Mira en bien. Y esto también era vanidad.
texts.ecc.2.2: A la risa dije: Enloqueces; y al placer: ¿De qué sirve esto?
texts.ecc.2.3: Yo propuse en mi corazón de atraer al vino mi carne, y que mi corazón anduviese en sabiduría, y retuviese la insensatez, hasta ver cual fuese el bien de los hijos de los hombres, en el cual se ocupasen debajo del cielo todos los días de su vida.
texts.ecc.2.4: Engrandecí mis obras, edifiquéme casas, plantéme viñas;
texts.ecc.2.5: Híceme huertos, y jardines; y planté en ellos árboles de todos frutos.
texts.ecc.2.6: Híceme estanques de aguas para regar de ellos el bosque donde crecían los árboles.
texts.ecc.2.7: Poseí siervos y siervas, y tuve hijos de familia: también tuve posesión grande de vacas y ovejas sobre todos los que fueron antes de mí en Jerusalem.
texts.ecc.2.8: Alleguéme también plata y oro, y tesoro preciado de reyes y de provincias. Híceme cantores, y cantoras; y todos los deleites de los hijos de los hombres, sinfonía y sinfonías.
texts.ecc.2.9: Y fui magnificado, y aumentado más que todos los que fueron antes de mí en Jerusalem: además de esto mi sabiduría me perseveró.
texts.ecc.2.10: No negué a mis ojos ninguna cosa que deseasen; ni aparté a mi corazón de toda alegría; porque mi corazón gozó de todo mi trabajo; y esta fue mi parte de todo mi trabajo.
texts.ecc.2.11: Al cabo yo miré todas las obras que habían hecho mis manos, y el trabajo que tomé para hacerlas; y, he aquí, todo vanidad y aflicción de espíritu; y que no hay más debajo del sol.
texts.ecc.2.12: ¶ Después yo torné a mirar para ver la sabiduría, y los desvaríos, y la insensatez: (porque, ¿qué hombre hay que pueda seguir al rey en lo que ya hicieron?)
texts.ecc.2.13: Y yo ví que la sabiduría sobrepuja a la insensatez, como la luz a las tinieblas.
texts.ecc.2.14: El sabio tiene sus ojos en su cabeza: mas el insensato anda en tinieblas. Y entendí también yo, que un mismo suceso sucederá al uno y al otro.
texts.ecc.2.15: Y yo dije en mi corazón: Como sucederá al insensato, me sucederá también a mí: ¿para qué pues he trabajado hasta ahora por hacerme más sabio? Y dije en mi corazón, que también esto era vanidad.
texts.ecc.2.16: Porque ni del sabio, ni del insensato, habrá memoria para siempre; porque en viniendo días ya todo será olvidado; y también morirá el sabio, como el insensato.
texts.ecc.2.17: Y aborrecí la vida; porque toda obra que se hacía debajo del sol, me era fastidiosa; porque todo era vanidad y aflicción de espíritu.
texts.ecc.2.18: Y yo aborrecí todo mi trabajo, en que trabajé debajo del sol: el cual dejaré a otro, que vendrá después de mí.
texts.ecc.2.19: ¿Y quién sabe si será sabio, o insensato, el que se enseñoreará en todo mi trabajo, en que ya trabajé, y en que me hice sabio debajo del sol? Esto también es vanidad.
texts.ecc.2.20: Y yo me torné para desesperar mi corazón, por todo el trabajo en que trabajé, y en que me hice sabio debajo del sol.
texts.ecc.2.21: Que trabaje el hombre con sabiduría, y con ciencia, y con rectitud, y que haya de dar su hacienda a hombre que nunca trabajó en ello. También esto es vanidad, y gran trabajo.
texts.ecc.2.22: Porque ¿qué tiene el hombre por todo su trabajo, y fatiga de su corazón, en que él trabajó debajo del sol?
texts.ecc.2.23: Porque todos sus días no son si no dolores, y enojos sus ocupaciones; aun de noche no reposa su corazón. Esto también es vanidad.
texts.ecc.2.24: ¶ No hay luego bien para el hombre si no que coma y beba, y que su alma vea el bien de su trabajo. También ví yo, que esto es de la mano de Dios.
texts.ecc.2.25: Porque ¿quién comerá; y quién se curará mejor que yo?
texts.ecc.2.26: Porque al hombre que es bueno delante de Dios, él le da sabiduría, y ciencia, y alegría: mas al pecador dio ocupación, que allegue, y amontone, para que dé al bueno delante de él. También esto es vanidad y aflicción de espíritu.
texts.ecc.3.1: Para todas las cosas hay sazón; y todo lo que quisiereis debajo del cielo, tiene su tiempo determinado.
texts.ecc.3.2: Tiempo de nacer, y tiempo de morir: tiempo de plantar, y tiempo de arrancar lo plantado:
texts.ecc.3.3: Tiempo de matar, y tiempo de curar: tiempo de destruir, y tiempo de edificar:
texts.ecc.3.4: Tiempo de llorar, y tiempo de reír: tiempo de endechar, y tiempo de bailar:
texts.ecc.3.5: Tiempo de esparcir las piedras, y tiempo de allegar las piedras: tiempo de abrazar, y tiempo de alejarse del abrazar:
texts.ecc.3.6: Tiempo de buscar, y tiempo de perder: tiempo de guardar, y tiempo de echar:
texts.ecc.3.7: Tiempo de romper, y tiempo de coser: tiempo de callar, y tiempo de hablar:
texts.ecc.3.8: Tiempo de amar, y tiempo de aborrecer: tiempo de guerra, y tiempo de paz.
texts.ecc.3.9: ¿Qué tiene más el que trabaja en lo que trabaja?
texts.ecc.3.10: Yo he visto la ocupación que Dios dio a los hijos de los hombres, para que en ella se ocupasen.
texts.ecc.3.11: Todo lo hizo hermoso en su tiempo, y aun el mundo dio a su corazón, de tal manera que no alcance el hombre esta obra de Dios desde el principio hasta el cabo.
texts.ecc.3.12: Yo he conocido que no hay mejor para ellos, que alegrarse, y hacer bien en su vida.
texts.ecc.3.13: Y también que es don de Dios, que todo hombre coma y beba, y goce de todo su trabajo.
texts.ecc.3.14: He entendido, que todo lo que Dios hace eso será perpetuo: sobre aquello no se añadirá, ni de ello se disminuirá; porque Dios hace, para que teman los hombres delante de él.
texts.ecc.3.15: Aquello que fue, ya es; y lo que ha de ser ya fue; y Dios restaura lo que pasó.
texts.ecc.3.16: ¶ Ví más debajo del sol: en lugar del juicio, allí la impiedad; y en lugar de la justicia, allí la iniquidad.
texts.ecc.3.17: Y yo dije en mi corazón: Al justo y al impío juzgará Dios, porque allí hay tiempo determinado a todo lo que quisiereis, y sobre todo lo que se hace.
texts.ecc.3.18: ¶ Dije en mi corazón acerca de la condición de los hijos de los hombres, que Dios los hizo escogidos; y es para ver, que ellos sean bestias los unos a los otros.
texts.ecc.3.19: Porque el suceso de los hijos de los hombres, y el suceso del animal, el mismo suceso es; como mueren los unos, así mueren los otros; y una misma respiración tienen todos; ni tiene más el hombre que la bestia; porque todo es vanidad.
texts.ecc.3.20: Todo va a un lugar; todo es hecho del polvo; y todo se tornará en el mismo polvo.
texts.ecc.3.21: ¿Quién sabe si el espíritu de los hijos de los hombres suba arriba, y el espíritu del animal descienda debajo de la tierra?
texts.ecc.3.22: Así que he visto que no hay bien, mas que alegrarse el hombre con lo que hiciere; porque esta es su parte: porque ¿quién le llevará para que vea lo que ha de ser después de él?
texts.ecc.4.1: Y tornéme yo, y ví todas las violencias que se hacen debajo del sol: y, he aquí las lágrimas de los oprimidos, y que no tienen quien los consuele; y que la fuerza estaba en la mano de sus opresores, y para ellos no había consolador.
texts.ecc.4.2: Y alabé yo los muertos, que ya murieron, más que los vivos, que son vivos hasta ahora.
texts.ecc.4.3: Y tuve por mejor que ellos ambos al que aun no fue; porque no ha visto las malas obras que se hacen debajo del sol.
texts.ecc.4.4: ¶ Ví también todo trabajo, y toda rectitud de obras, que no es sino envidia del hombre contra su prójimo. También esto es vanidad, y aflicción de espíritu.
texts.ecc.4.5: El insensato pliega sus manos, y come su carne.
texts.ecc.4.6: Mas vale el un puño lleno con descanso, que ambos puños llenos con trabajo, y aflicción de espíritu.
texts.ecc.4.7: ¶ Yo me torné otra vez, y ví otra vanidad debajo del sol.
texts.ecc.4.8: Es el hombre solo, sin sucesor; que ni tiene hijo ni hermano, y nunca cesa de trabajar, ni aun sus ojos se hartan de sus riquezas; ni piensa: ¿Para quién trabajo yo, y defraudo mi alma del bien? También esto es vanidad, y ocupación mala.
texts.ecc.4.9: Mejores son dos que uno; porque tienen mejor paga de su trabajo.
texts.ecc.4.10: Porque si cayeren, el uno levantará a su compañero: mas ¡ay del solo! que cuando cayere, no habrá segundo que le levante.
texts.ecc.4.11: También si dos durmieren, calentarse han: mas el solo ¿cómo se calentará?
texts.ecc.4.12: Y si alguno prevaleciere contra el uno, dos estarán contra él; porque cordón de tres dobleces no presto se rompe.
texts.ecc.4.13: ¶ Mejor es el muchacho pobre y sabio, que el rey viejo e insensato, que no puede ser más avisado.
texts.ecc.4.14: Porque como de la cárcel salió a reinar; porque en su reino nació pobre.
texts.ecc.4.15: Ví mas todos los vivientes debajo del sol caminando con el muchacho sucesor, que estará en su lugar.
texts.ecc.4.16: No tiene fin todo el pueblo, que fue antes de ellos: tampoco los que fueren después, se alegrarán en él. También esto es vanidad, y aflicción de espíritu.
texts.ecc.5.1: Cuando fueres a la casa de Dios, mira bien por tu pie; y acércate más para oír, que para dar el sacrificio de los insensatos; porque no saben que hacen mal.
texts.ecc.5.2: No te des priesa con tu boca, ni tu corazón se apresure a pronunciar palabra delante de Dios; porque Dios está en el cielo, y tú sobre la tierra: por tanto tus palabras sean pocas.
texts.ecc.5.3: Porque como de la mucha ocupación viene el sueño, así la voz del insensato, de la multitud de las palabras.
texts.ecc.5.4: Cuando a Dios prometieres promesa no tardes de pagarla; porque no se agrada de los insensatos. Lo que prometieres, paga.
texts.ecc.5.5: Mejor es que no prometas, que no que prometas, y no pagues.
texts.ecc.5.6: No sueltes tu boca para hacer pecar a tu carne; ni digas delante del ángel, que fue ignorancia: ¿por qué harás tú que se aire Dios a causa de tu voz, y que destruya la obra de tus manos?
texts.ecc.5.7: Porque los sueños son en multitud; y las vanidades y las palabras son muchas: mas teme a Dios.
texts.ecc.5.8: ¶ Si violencias de pobres, y extorsión de derecho y de justicia vieres en la provincia, no te maravilles de esta licencia; porque alto está mirando sobre alto, y más altos están sobre ellos:
texts.ecc.5.9: Y mayor altura hay en todas las cosas de la tierra: mas el que sirve al campo es rey.
texts.ecc.5.10: ¶ El que ama el dinero, no se hartará de dinero; y el que ama el mucho tener, no tendrá fruto. También esto es vanidad.
texts.ecc.5.11: Cuando los bienes se aumentan, también se aumentan sus comedores: ¿qué bien pues tendrá su dueño sino ver los de sus ojos?
texts.ecc.5.12: Dulce es el sueño del trabajador, que coma mucho, que poco: mas al rico, la hartura no le deja dormir.
texts.ecc.5.13: Hay otra trabajosa enfermedad que ví debajo del sol: las riquezas guardadas de sus dueños para su mal,
texts.ecc.5.14: Las cuales se pierden en malas ocupaciones; y a los hijos que engendraron nada les quedó en la mano:
texts.ecc.5.15: Como salió del vientre de su madre, desnudo, así se vuelve, tornando como vino, y nada tuvo de su trabajo para llevar en su mano.
texts.ecc.5.16: Este también es un gran mal, que como vino, así se haya de volver. ¿Y de qué le aprovechó trabajar al viento?
texts.ecc.5.17: Además de esto, todos los días de su vida comerá en tinieblas, y mucho enojo, y dolor, e ira.
texts.ecc.5.18: ¶ He aquí pues el bien que yo he visto: Que lo bueno es comer, y beber, y gozar del bien de todo su trabajo, con que trabaja debajo del sol todos los días de su vida, que Dios le dio; porque esta es su parte.
texts.ecc.5.19: Y también, que a todo hombre, a quien Dios dio riquezas, y hacienda, también le dio facultad para que coma de ellas, y tome su parte, y goce su trabajo: esto es don de Dios.
texts.ecc.5.20: Porque no se acordará mucho de los días de su vida, porque Dios le responderá con alegría de su corazón.
texts.ecc.6.1: Hay otro mal que he visto debajo del cielo, y muy común entre los hombres:
texts.ecc.6.2: Hombre, a quien Dios dio riquezas, y hacienda, y honra, y nada le falta de todo lo que su alma desea; y Dios no le dio facultad de comer de ello; antes los extraños se lo comen: esto vanidad es, y enfermedad trabajosa.
texts.ecc.6.3: Si el hombre engendrare cien hijos, y viviere muchos años, y los días de su edad fueren asaz; si su alma no se hartó del bien, y también careció de sepultura; yo digo que el abortivo es mejor que él.
texts.ecc.6.4: Porque en vano vino, y a tinieblas va, y con tinieblas será cubierto su nombre.
texts.ecc.6.5: Aunque no haya visto el sol, ni conocido nada, más reposo tiene este, que aquel.
texts.ecc.6.6: Porque si viviere mil años dos veces, y no gozó del bien; cierto todos van a un lugar.
texts.ecc.6.7: Todo el trabajo del hombre es para su boca, y con todo eso, su deseo no se harta.
texts.ecc.6.8: Porque ¿qué más tiene el sabio que el insensato? ¿Qué más tiene el pobre que supo caminar entre los vivos?
texts.ecc.6.9: Mas vale vista de ojos, que deseo que pasa; y también esto es vanidad, y aflicción de espíritu.
texts.ecc.6.10: ¶ El que es, ya su nombre ha sido nombrado, y se sabe, que es hombre; y que no podrá contender con el que es más fuerte que él.
texts.ecc.6.11: Ciertamente las muchas palabras multiplican la vanidad. ¿Qué más tiene el hombre?
texts.ecc.6.12: Porque ¿quién sabe cual es el bien del hombre en la vida todos los días de la vida de su vanidad, que los pasa como sombra? Porque ¿quién enseñará al hombre que será después de él debajo del sol?
texts.ecc.7.1: Mejor es la buena fama que el buen ungüento; y el día de la muerte, que el día del nacer mismo.
texts.ecc.7.2: Mejor es ir a la casa del luto que a la casa del convite; porque es el fin de todos los hombres; y el que vive, lo pondrá en su corazón.
texts.ecc.7.3: Mejor es el enojo que la risa; porque con la tristeza del rostro se enmendará el corazón.
texts.ecc.7.4: El corazón de los sabios, en la casa del luto: mas el corazón de los insensatos, en la casa del placer.
texts.ecc.7.5: Mejor es oír la reprensión del sabio, que la canción de los insensatos.
texts.ecc.7.6: Porque la risa del insensato es como el estrépito de las espinas debajo de la olla; y también esto es vanidad.
texts.ecc.7.7: Ciertamente el agravio hace enloquecer al sabio; y el presente corrompe el corazón.
texts.ecc.7.8: Mejor es el fin del negocio, que su principio: mejor es el sufrido de espíritu, que el altivo de espíritu.
texts.ecc.7.9: No te apresures en tu espíritu a enojarte; porque la ira en el seno de los insensatos reposa.
texts.ecc.7.10: Nunca digas: ¿Qué es la causa que los tiempos pasados fueron mejores que estos? Porque nunca de esto preguntarás con sabiduría.
texts.ecc.7.11: Buena es la ciencia con herencia; y más a los que ven el sol:
texts.ecc.7.12: Porque en la sombra de la ciencia, y en la sombra del dinero reposa el hombre; mas la sabiduría excede, en que da vida a sus poseedores.
texts.ecc.7.13: Mira la obra de Dios; porque ¿quién podrá enderezar el que él torció?
texts.ecc.7.14: En el día del bien, está en el bien; y en el día del mal, vé. Dios también hizo esto delante de lo otro, porque el hombre no halle nada tras de él.
texts.ecc.7.15: ¶ Todo lo ví en los días de mi vanidad. Justo hay, que perece por su justicia; e impío hay, que por su maldad alarga sus días.
texts.ecc.7.16: No seas justo mucho, ni seas demasiadamente sabio: ¿por qué te destruirás?
texts.ecc.7.17: No hagas mal mucho, ni seas insensato: ¿por qué morirás antes de tu tiempo?
texts.ecc.7.18: Bueno es que tomes esto, y también de estotro no apartes tu mano; porque el que a Dios teme, saldrá con todo.
texts.ecc.7.19: La sabiduría esfuerza al sabio, más que diez poderosos príncipes, que sean en la ciudad.
texts.ecc.7.20: Ciertamente no hay hombre justo en la tierra, que haga bien, y nunca peque.
texts.ecc.7.21: Tampoco apliques tu corazón a todas las palabras que se hablaren; porque alguna vez no oigas a tu siervo, que dice mal de ti.
texts.ecc.7.22: Porque tu corazón sabe, que tú también dijiste mal de otros muchas veces.
texts.ecc.7.23: ¶ Todas estas cosas probé con sabiduría, diciendo: Hacerme he sabio: mas ella se alejó de mí.
texts.ecc.7.24: Lejos está lo que fue; y lo profundo profundo ¿quién lo hallará?
texts.ecc.7.25: Yo he rodeado, y mi corazón, por saber, y examinar, e inquirir la sabiduría, y la razón; y por saber la maldad de la insensatez, y el desvarío del error,
texts.ecc.7.26: Y yo he hallado más amarga que la muerte la mujer: la cual es redes, y lazos su corazón: sus manos, ligaduras. El bueno delante de Dios escapará de ella: mas el pecador será preso en ella.
texts.ecc.7.27: Mira, esto he hallado, dice el Predicador, mirando las cosas una a una para hallar la razón:
texts.ecc.7.28: Lo cual mucho buscó mi alma, y no lo hallé: un hombre entre mil he hallado: mas mujer de todas estas nunca hallé.
texts.ecc.7.29: Solamente, he aquí, esto hallé: que Dios hizo al hombre recto: mas ellos buscaron muchas cuentas.
texts.ecc.8.1: ¿Quién como el sabio? ¿Y quién como el que sabe la declaración de la palabra? La sabiduría del hombre hará relucir su rostro, y la fuerza de su cara se mudará.
texts.ecc.8.2: ¶ Yo te aviso que guardes el mandamiento del rey, y la palabra del juramento de Dios.
texts.ecc.8.3: No te apresures a irte de delante de él: ni estés en cosa mala, porque él hará todo lo que quisiere.
texts.ecc.8.4: Porque la palabra del rey es su potestad; y quién le dirá: ¿Qué haces?
texts.ecc.8.5: ¶ El que guarda el mandamiento, no experimentará mal; y el tiempo, y el juicio, conoce el corazón del sabio.
texts.ecc.8.6: Porque para todo lo que quisiereis hay tiempo, y juicio; porque el trabajo del hombre es grande sobre él.
texts.ecc.8.7: Porque no sabe lo que ha de ser, y cuando haya de ser, ¿quién se lo enseñara?
texts.ecc.8.8: No hay hombre que tenga potestad sobre su espíritu para detener el espíritu; ni hay potestad sobre el día de la muerte; ni hay armas en guerra; ni la impiedad escapará al que la posee.
texts.ecc.8.9: ¶ Todo esto he visto, y he puesto mi corazón en todo lo que se hace debajo del sol, el tiempo en que el hombre se enseñorea del hombre para mal suyo.
texts.ecc.8.10: Entonces ví también impíos, que después de sepultados, volvieron; y los que de lugar santo caminaron, fueron puestos en olvido en la ciudad donde obraron verdad: esto también vanidad es.
texts.ecc.8.11: Porque luego no se ejecuta sentencia sobre la mala obra, el corazón de los hijos de los hombres está lleno en ellos para hacer mal.
texts.ecc.8.12: Porque el que peca, haga mal cien veces, y le sea prolongado, aun yo también sé, que los que a Dios temen, tendrán bien, los que temieren delante de su presencia;
texts.ecc.8.13: Y que el impío nunca tendrá bien, ni le serán prolongados los días, mas serán como sombra; porque no temió delante de la presencia de Dios.
texts.ecc.8.14: Hay otra vanidad que se hace sobre la tierra: que hay justos, los cuales son pagados como si hicieran obras de impíos; y hay impíos, que son pagados como si hicieran obras de justos. Digo que esto también es vanidad.
texts.ecc.8.15: ¶ Por tanto yo alabé la alegría: que no tiene el hombre bien debajo del sol, sino que coma, y beba, y se alegre; y que esto se le pegue de su trabajo los días de su vida, que Dios le dio debajo del sol.
texts.ecc.8.16: Por lo cual yo di mi corazón a conocer sabiduría, y a ver la ocupación que se hace sobre la tierra: que ni de noche, ni de día, ve el hombre sueño en sus ojos.
texts.ecc.8.17: Y ví acerca de todas las obras de Dios, que el hombre no puede alcanzar obra que se haga debajo del sol; por la cual trabaja el hombre buscándola, y no la hallará: aunque diga el sabio que sabe, no la hallará: aunque diga el sabio que sabe, no la podrá alcanzar.
texts.ecc.9.1: Ciertamente a todo esto di mi corazón, para declarar todo esto: Que los justos, y los sabios, y sus obras, están en la mano de Dios: y que no sabe el hombre ni el amor, ni el odio, por todo lo que pasa delante de él.
texts.ecc.9.2: ¶ Todo acontece de la misma manera a todos: un mismo suceso tiene el justo y el impío; el bueno, y el limpio, y el no limpio; y el que sacrifica, y el que no sacrifica; como el bueno así el que peca: el que jura, como el que teme el juramento.
texts.ecc.9.3: Este mal hay entre todo lo que se hace debajo del sol: que todos tengan un mismo suceso; y que también el corazón de los hijos de los hombres esté lleno de mal, y de enloquecimiento en su corazón en su vida, y después, a los muertos.
texts.ecc.9.4: Porque para todo aquel que está aun entre los vivos, hay esperanza; porque mejor es perro vivo, que león muerto.
texts.ecc.9.5: Porque los que viven, saben que han de morir: mas los muertos nada saben, ni más tienen paga; porque su memoria es puesta en olvido.
texts.ecc.9.6: Aun su amor, su odio, y su envidia ya feneció; y no tienen ya más parte en el siglo, en todo lo que se hace debajo del sol.
texts.ecc.9.7: Anda, y come tu pan con gozo, y bebe tu vino con alegre corazón; porque tus obras ya son agradables a Dios.
texts.ecc.9.8: En todo tiempo sean blancos tus vestidos; y nunca falte ungüento sobre tu cabeza.
texts.ecc.9.9: Goza de la vida con la mujer que amas, todos los días de la vida de tu vanidad, que te son dados debajo del sol, todos los días de tu vanidad; porque esta es tu parte en la vida, y en tu trabajo, en que trabajas debajo del sol.
texts.ecc.9.10: Todo lo que te viniere a la mano para hacer, házlo según tus fuerzas; porque en el sepulcro, donde tú vas, no hay obra, ni industria, ni ciencia, ni sabiduría.
texts.ecc.9.11: ¶ Tornéme, y ví debajo del sol, que ni es de los ligeros la carrera; ni la guerra, de los fuertes; ni aun de los sabios el pan; ni de los prudentes las riquezas; ni de los elocuentes la gracia: mas que tiempo, y ocasión acontece a todos.
texts.ecc.9.12: Porque el hombre tampoco conoce su tiempo: como los peces, que son presos en la mala red, y como las aves, que se prenden en lazo; así son enlazados los hijos de los hombres en el tiempo malo, cuando cae de súbito sobre ellos.
texts.ecc.9.13: ¶ También ví esta sabiduría debajo del sol; la cual me es grande:
texts.ecc.9.14: Una pequeña ciudad, y pocos hombres en ella; y viene contra ella un gran rey, y cércala, y edifica contra ella grandes baluartes:
texts.ecc.9.15: Y hállase en ella un hombre pobre, sabio, el cual escapa la ciudad con su sabiduría; y nadie se acordaba de aquel pobre hombre.
texts.ecc.9.16: Entonces yo dije: Mejor es la sabiduría que la fortaleza, aunque la ciencia del pobre sea menospreciada, y sus palabras no sean escuchadas.
texts.ecc.9.17: Las palabras del sabio con reposo son oídas, más que el clamor del señor entre los insensatos.
texts.ecc.9.18: Mejor es la sabiduría que las armas de guerra: mas un pecador destruye mucho bien.
texts.ecc.10.1: Las moscas muertas hacen heder y dar mal olor el perfume del perfumador; y al estimado por sabiduría y honra una pequeña insensatez.
texts.ecc.10.2: El corazón del sabio está a su mano derecha: mas el corazón del insensato, a su mano izquierda.
texts.ecc.10.3: Y aun cuando el insensato va por el camino, su cordura falta; y dice a todos: insensato es.
texts.ecc.10.4: Si espíritu de señor te acometiere, no dejes tu lugar; porque la flojedad hará reposar grandes pecados.
texts.ecc.10.5: ¶ Hay otro mal que ví debajo del sol, como salido de delante del señor por yerro:
texts.ecc.10.6: La insensatez está asentada en grandes alturas; y los ricos están sentados en bajeza.
texts.ecc.10.7: Ví siervos encima de caballos, y príncipes que andaban, como siervos, a tierra.
texts.ecc.10.8: ¶ El que hiciere el hoyo, caerá en él; y el que aportillare el vallado, morderle ha la serpiente.
texts.ecc.10.9: El que mudare las piedras, tendrá trabajo en ellas: el que cortare la leña, peligrará en ella.
texts.ecc.10.10: Si se embotare el hierro, y su filo no fuere aguzado, añadir más fuerza: mas la bondad de la sabiduría excede.
texts.ecc.10.11: Si la serpiente mordiere no encantada, no es más el lenguaz.
texts.ecc.10.12: Las palabras de la boca del sabio son gracia: mas los labios del insensato lo echan a perder.
texts.ecc.10.13: El principio de las palabras de su boca es insensatez; y el fin de su habla, desvarío malo.
texts.ecc.10.14: El insensato multiplica palabras, y dice: No sabe hombre lo que ha de ser: ¿y quién le hará saber, lo que será después de él?
texts.ecc.10.15: El trabajo de los insensatos los fatiga; porque no saben por donde van a la ciudad.
texts.ecc.10.16: ¶ ¡Ay de ti tierra, cuando tu rey fuere mozo, y tus príncipes comen de mañana!
texts.ecc.10.17: ¡Bienaventurada tierra tú, cuando tu rey fuere hijo de nobles, y tus príncipes comen a su hora por la fuerza, y no por el beber!
texts.ecc.10.18: ¶ Por la pereza se cae la techumbre; y por la flojedad de manos se llueve la casa.
texts.ecc.10.19: Por el placer se hace el convite, y el vino alegra los vivos; y el dinero responde a todo.
texts.ecc.10.20: Ni aun en tu pensamiento digas mal del rey; ni en los secretos de tu cámara digas mal del rico; porque las aves del cielo llevarán la voz; y las que tienen alas, harán saber la palabra.
texts.ecc.11.1: Echa tu pan sobre las aguas, que después de muchos días lo hallarás.
texts.ecc.11.2: Reparte a siete, y aun a ocho; porque no sabes el mal que vendrá sobre la tierra.
texts.ecc.11.3: Si las nubes fueren llenas de agua, sobre la tierra la derramarán; y si el árbol cayere al mediodía o al norte, al lugar que el árbol cayere, allí quedará.
texts.ecc.11.4: El que al viento mira, nunca sembrará; y el que mira a las nubes, nunca segará.
texts.ecc.11.5: Como tú no sabes cual es el camino del viento, o como se crían los huesos en el vientre de la mujer preñada, así ignoras la obra de Dios, el cual hace todas las cosas.
texts.ecc.11.6: Por la mañana siembra tu simiente, y a la tarde no dejes reposar tu mano: porque tú no sabes cual es lo mejor, esto, o lo otro, o si ambas a dos cosas son buenas.
texts.ecc.11.7: ¶ Suave ciertamente es la luz, y agradable es a los ojos ver el sol:
texts.ecc.11.8: Mas si el hombre viviere muchos años, y en todos ellos hubiere tenido alegría: si después trajere a la memoria los días de las tinieblas, que serán muchos; todo lo que le habrá pasado, dirá haber sido vanidad.
texts.ecc.11.9: Alégrate mancebo en tu mocedad, y tome placer tu corazón en los días de tu juventud; y camina en los caminos de tu corazón, y en la vista de tus ojos: mas sabe, que sobre todas estas cosas te traerá Dios en juicio.
texts.ecc.11.10: Quita pues el enojo de tu corazón, y aparta de tu carne el mal; porque la mocedad y la juventud vanidad es.
texts.ecc.12.1: Y ten memoria de tu Criador en los días de tu juventud, antes que vengan los malos días, y lleguen los años, de los cuales digas: No tengo en ellos contentamiento.
texts.ecc.12.2: Antes que se oscurezca el sol, y la luz, y la luna, y las estrellas; y las nubes se tornen tras la lluvia:
texts.ecc.12.3: Cuando temblarán las guardas de la casa, y se encorvarán los hombres fuertes, y cesarán las muelas, y se disminuirán; y se oscurecerán los que miran por las ventanas;
texts.ecc.12.4: Y las puertas de afuera se cerrarán por la bajeza de la voz de la muela; y se levantará a la voz del ave, y todas las hijas de canción serán humilladas:
texts.ecc.12.5: Cuando también temerán de lo alto, y los tropezones en el camino; y florecerá el almendro, y cargarse ha la langosta, y perderse ha el apetito; porque el hombre va a la casa de su siglo, y los endechadores por la plaza andarán en derredor.
texts.ecc.12.6: Antes que la cadena de plata se quiebre, y se rompa la lenteja de oro, y el cántaro se quiebre junto a la fuente, y la rueda sea rompida sobre el pozo;
texts.ecc.12.7: Y el polvo se torne a la tierra, como era antes, y el espíritu se vuelva a Dios, que le dio.
texts.ecc.12.8: ¶ Vanidad de vanidades, dijo el Predicador, todo vanidad.
texts.ecc.12.9: Y cuanto más el Predicador fue sabio, tanto más enseñó sabiduría al pueblo, e hizo escuchar, e hizo escudriñar; y compuso muchos proverbios.
texts.ecc.12.10: Procuró el Predicador hallar palabras agradables, y escritura recta, palabras de verdad.
texts.ecc.12.11: Las palabras de los sabios son como aguijones, y como clavos hincados de los maestros de las congregaciones, puestas debajo de un pastor.
texts.ecc.12.12: Y además de esto, hijo mío, sé avisado: no hay fin de hacer muchos libros; y el mucho estudio aflicción es de la carne.
texts.ecc.12.13: El fin de todo el sermón es oído: teme a Dios, y guarda sus mandamientos, porque esto es el todo del hombre.
texts.ecc.12.14: Porque Dios traerá toda obra en juicio, el cual se hará sobre toda cosa oculta, buena, o mala.

texts.ecc.1.1: The words of the Proclaimer, son of David, king in Jerusalem.
texts.ecc.1.2: Vanity of vanities! saith the Proclaimer, vanity of vanities! all, is vanity.
texts.ecc.1.3: What profit hath Man, in all his toil wherewith he toileth under the sun?
texts.ecc.1.4: Generation, goeth and, generation, cometh, but, the earth, unto times age-abiding, remaineth.
texts.ecc.1.5: And the sun, breaketh forth, and the sun, goeth in,—yea, unto his own place, he panteth, from whence he brake forth.
texts.ecc.1.6: Going unto the south, and circling unto the north,—circling, circling continually, is, the wind, and, over its own circuits, returneth the wind.
texts.ecc.1.7: All the streams, flow into the sea, yet, the sea, is not full,—unto the place whither the streams flow, thither, do they again flow.
texts.ecc.1.8: All words, are weak, unable is any man to tell,—not satisfied is the eye by seeing, nor filled is the ear with hearing.
texts.ecc.1.9: That which hath been, is the same that shall be, and, that which hath been done, is the same that shall be done,—and there is, nothing new, under the sun.
texts.ecc.1.10: Is there a thing, of which it can be said, See here, it is, new? Already, hath it been, for ages, [it is something] which was before us.
texts.ecc.1.11: There is, no remembrance, of the thing before,—nor, even of the things after, which shall be, will there be any remembrance, with them who shall come after.
texts.ecc.1.12: I, the Proclaimer, was king over Israel, in Jerusalem.
texts.ecc.1.13: And I gave my heart to seek and to search out, wisely, concerning all things which are done under the heavens,—the same, is the vexatious employment God hath given to the sons of men, to work toilsomely therein,
texts.ecc.1.14: I saw all the works which were done under the sun,—and lo! all, was vanity, and a feeding on wind.
texts.ecc.1.15: That which is crooked, cannot be straight,—and, that which is wanting, cannot be reckoned.
texts.ecc.1.16: Spake, I, in my heart, saying, As for me, lo! I have become great, and have gathered wisdom, beyond any one who hath been before me over Jerusalem,—and, my heart, hath seen much wisdom and knowledge:
texts.ecc.1.17: yea I have given my heart, to know wisdom, and to know madness, and folly,—I know that, even this, is a feeding on wind.
texts.ecc.1.18: For, in much wisdom, is much vexation,—and, he that increaseth knowledge, increaseth pain.
texts.ecc.2.1: Said, I, in my heart, Come now! I will prove thee with gladness, and look thou on blessedness,—but lo! even that, was vanity.
texts.ecc.2.2: Of laughter, I said, Madness! and, of mirth, What can it do?
texts.ecc.2.3: I sought out with my heart, to cherish with wine, my flesh,—but, my heart, was to guide with wisdom, even in laying hold of folly, until I should see which was blessedness for the sons of men, as to that which they could do, under the heavens, during the number of the days of their life.
texts.ecc.2.4: I enlarged my works,—I built me houses, I planted me vineyards;
texts.ecc.2.5: I made me gardens, and parks,—I planted in them trees of every kind of fruit;
texts.ecc.2.6: I made me pools of water,—to irrigate therefrom the thick-set saplings growing up into trees:
texts.ecc.2.7: I acquired, men-servants and women-servants, and, the children of the household, were mine,—also possessions, herds and flocks in abundance, were mine, beyond all who had been before me in Jerusalem;
texts.ecc.2.8: I heaped me up, both silver and gold, and the peculiar treasure of kings, and provinces,—I provided me singing-men and singing-women, and the delights of the sons of men, a wife and wives.
texts.ecc.2.9: So I became great, and increased, more than any one who had been before me in Jerusalem,—moreover, my wisdom, remained with me;
texts.ecc.2.10: and, nothing that mine eyes asked, withheld I from them,—I did not keep back my heart from any gladness, for, my heart, obtained gladness out of all my toil, and so, this, was my portion, out of all my toil.
texts.ecc.2.11: When, I, looked upon all my works, which my hands had made, and on my toil, whereon I had toilsomely wrought, then lo! all, was vanity, and feeding on wind, and there was no profit under the sun.
texts.ecc.2.12: Thus turned, I, to look at wisdom, and madness and folly,—for what can the man [do more] who cometh after the king? [save] that which, already, men have done.
texts.ecc.2.13: Then saw, I, that wisdom doth excel folly,—as far as light excelleth darkness.
texts.ecc.2.14: As for the wise man, his eyes, are in his head, whereas, the dullard, in darkness, doth walk,—but, I myself, knew that, one destiny, happeneth to them, all.
texts.ecc.2.15: Then said, I, in my heart, As it happeneth to the dullard, even to me, will it happen, but wherefore, then, became, I, wise to excess? Therefore spake I, in my heart, Even this, is vanity.
texts.ecc.2.16: For there is no remembrance of a wise man, more than of a dullard, unto times age-abiding,—seeing that, already, in the days to come, all hath been forgotten, how then cometh it that the wise man dieth equally with the dullard?
texts.ecc.2.17: Therefore I hated life, for, a vexation unto me, was the work which was done under the sun,—for, all, was vanity, and a feeding on wind.
texts.ecc.2.18: Therefore hated, I, all my toil, wherein I was toiling, under the sun,—in that I should leave it for the man who should come after me;
texts.ecc.2.19: and who could know whether a, wise man, he would be or a foolish, and yet he would lord it over all my toil, wherein I had toiled and wherein I had acted wisely, under the sun,—even this, was vanity.
texts.ecc.2.20: Then resolved I, to give my heart over to despair,—concerning all the toil, wherein I had toiled, under the sun.
texts.ecc.2.21: For here is a man, whose toil hath been with wisdom and with knowledge and with skill,—yet, to a man who hath not toiled therein, shall he leave it as his portion, even this, was vanity and a great vexation.
texts.ecc.2.22: For what hath the man for all his toil, and for the striving of his heart,—wherein, he himself, toiled under the sun?
texts.ecc.2.23: For, all his days, are pains, and, vexatious, is his employment, even in the night, his heart lieth not down,—even this, was, vanity.
texts.ecc.2.24: There was nothing more blessed for Man [than] that he should eat and drink, and see his desireth for blessedness in his toil,—even this, saw, I myself, that, from the hand of God, it was.
texts.ecc.2.25: For who could eat and who could enjoy, so well as I?
texts.ecc.2.26: For, to a man who is good before him, hath he given wisdom and knowledge and gladness,—whereas, to the sinner, he hath given employment, to gather and heap up, to give to one who is good before God, even this, was vanity, and a feeding on wind.
texts.ecc.3.1: For, every thing, there is a season,—and a time for every pursuit, under the heavens:—
texts.ecc.3.2: A time to be born, and a time to die,—A time to plant, and a time to uproot what is planted;
texts.ecc.3.3: A time to kill, and a time to heal,—A time to break down, and a time to build up;
texts.ecc.3.4: A time to weep, and a time to laugh,—A time to wail, and a time to dance for joy;
texts.ecc.3.5: A time to cast away stones, and a time to heap up stones,—A time to embrace, and a time to be far from loving embrace;
texts.ecc.3.6: A time to seek, and a time to give up as lost,—A time to keep, and a time to cast away;
texts.ecc.3.7: A time to rend, and a time to sew,—A time to be silent, and a time to speak;
texts.ecc.3.8: A time to love and a time to hate,—A time of war, and a time of peace.
texts.ecc.3.9: What profit hath he that worketh, in that wherein, himself, hath toiled?
texts.ecc.3.10: I looked at the employment which God hath given to the sons of men, to work therein:
texts.ecc.3.11: Everything, hath he made beautiful in its own time,—also, intelligence, hath he put in their heart, without which men could not find out the work which God hath wrought, from the beginning even unto the end.
